preface.p: Navigation Act 2012
Compilation date: 15 February 2025
Includes amendments: Act No. 2, 2025
This is a compilation of the Navigation Act 2012 that shows the text of the law as amended and in force on 15 February 2025 (the compilation date).
The notes at the end of this compilation (the endnotes) include information about amending laws and the amendment history of provisions of the compiled law.

The effect of uncommenced amendments is not shown in the text of the compiled law. Any uncommenced amendments affecting the law are accessible on the Register (www.legislation.gov.au). The details of amendments made up to, but not commenced at, the compilation date are underlined in the endnotes. For more information on any uncommenced amendments, see the Register for the compiled law.

p.b: Application, saving and transitional provisions for provisions and amendments

preface.p: If the operation of a provision or amendment of the compiled law is affected by an application, saving or transitional provision that is not included in this compilation, details are included in the endnotes.
For more information about any editorial changes made in this compilation, see the endnotes.

If the compiled law is modified by another law, the compiled law operates as modified but the modification does not amend the text of the law. Accordingly, this compilation does not show the text of the compiled law as modified. For more information on any modifications, see the Register for the compiled law.
If a provision of the compiled law has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law, details are included in the endnotes.

part.heading: Objects and simplified outline of Act

section.heading: Objects of Act

content.p: The objects of this Act are:
to promote the safety of life at sea; and
to promote safe navigation; and
to prevent pollution of the marine environment; and
to ensure that AMSA has the necessary power to carry out inspections of vessels and enforce national and international standards.

section.heading: Simplified outline of this Act

content.p: Overview of this Act
This Act is about maritime safety, seafarers and the prevention of pollution of the marine environment. It provides for matters relating to the following:
seafarers (Chapter 2);
the safety of regulated Australian vessels and foreign vessels (Chapter 3);
prevention of pollution (Chapter 4);
tonnage (Chapter 5);
the safety of navigation (Chapter 6);
wrecks and salvage (Chapter 7);
complying with, and enforcing, this Act (Chapter 8);
other general matters that relate to the above (Chapter 9).
Overview of the rest of this Chapter
The rest of this Chapter deals with:
the application of this Act, including how it interacts with certain State and Territory laws and its geographical application (Part 3); and
definitions that are used in this Act (Part 4); and
provisions that enable a vessel that would not otherwise be a regulated Australian vessel to opt in to coverage (Part 5).

part.heading: Provisions relating to the application of this Act

section.heading: Extension to Territories

content.p: This Act extends to every external Territory.

section.heading: Extraterritorial operation of Act

content.p: This Act applies both within and outside Australia.

section.heading: Act to bind the Crown

content.p: This Act binds the Crown in each of its capacities.
Nothing in this Act makes the Crown liable to a pecuniary penalty or to be prosecuted for an offence.

section.heading: Geographical jurisdiction for offences

content.p: Section 15.3 of the Criminal Code (extended geographical jurisdiction—category C) applies to all offences against this Act.

section.heading: Geographical application of offences and civil penalty provisions relating to foreign vessels, etc.

content.p: Despite sections 6 and 8, the master or owner of a foreign vessel, or a recreational vessel that does not have Australian nationality, does not:
commit an offence against this Act that relates to the vessel; or
contravene a civil penalty provision of this Act that relates to the vessel;
unless, at the time when the conduct constituting the alleged offence or contravention occurs, the vessel is:
in an Australian port; or
entering or leaving an Australian port; or
in the internal waters of Australia; or
in the territorial sea of Australia, other than in the course of innocent passage.
Note: Certain provisions of this Act provide that this section does not apply to specified offences and civil penalty provisions.

section.heading: Act does not apply to naval vessels etc.

content.p: This Act does not apply to, or in relation to:
a warship or other vessel that:
is operated for naval or military purposes by Australia or a foreign country; and
is under the command of a member of the Australian Defence Force or of a member of the armed forces of the foreign country; and
bears external marks of nationality; and
is manned by seafarers under armed forces discipline (however described); or
a Government vessel that is used only on government non-commercial service as a naval auxiliary; or
a vessel used by a foreign country for customs or law enforcement purposes.

section.heading: Application of Act to certain Australian Border Force vessels

content.p: An Australian Border Force vessel that would, apart from this section, not comply with a provision of Chapter 2, 3 or 6, or a person who would, apart from this section, not comply with a provision of those Chapters in relation to an Australian Border Force vessel, is taken to comply with that provision if:
(a) there is a document (the Australian Border Force vessel management plan) that:
has been prepared, reviewed and accepted in accordance with the regulations; and
relates to the Australian Border Force vessel or person; and
specifies requirements to be met by the Australian Border Force vessel or the person in relation to that provision; and
the Australian Border Force vessel or the person complies with the requirements of the Australian Border Force vessel management plan in relation to that provision.

section.heading: Provisions that give effect to various conventions

content.p: A provision of this Act that gives effect to a provision of:
the Safety Convention; or
the Prevention of Pollution Convention; or
the Prevention of Collisions Convention (in relation to an area other than the high seas); or
the Maritime Labour Convention;
does not apply in relation to a domestic commercial vessel, or a recreational vessel that has Australian nationality, when the vessel is in an area if:
a provision of the Marine Safety (Domestic Commercial Vessel) National Law gives effect to that provision of the Convention in relation to that vessel when it is in that area; or
if paragraph (d) does not apply—a provision of a law of a State or the Northern Territory gives effect to that provision of the Convention in relation to that vessel when it is in that area.

section.heading: Provisions that give effect to the Container Convention

content.p: Regulations giving effect to the Container Convention do not apply in relation to a container in a State or in the Northern Territory to the extent that a law of that State or Territory, as the case may be, makes provision giving effect to that Convention in relation to that container.

Structural safety requirements or tests that are not required or permitted by the Container Convention to be imposed on containers to which that Convention applies are not to be imposed by or under a law of a State or Territory on such containers.
