section.heading: Definition of regulated Australian vessel

content.p: (1) A vessel is a regulated Australian vessel if:
(a) under the Shipping Registration Act 1981, the vessel is registered, required to be registered or exempt under section 13 of that Act from that requirement; and
the vessel is not a recreational vessel; and
any of the following apply:
the vessel is proceeding on an overseas voyage or is for use on an overseas voyage;
a certificate issued under this Act, other than a non-Convention tonnage certificate or a certificate prescribed by the regulations, is in force for the vessel;
an opt-in declaration is in force for the vessel.
(2) A vessel is a regulated Australian vessel if the vessel is an Australian Border Force vessel.
A vessel referred to in subparagraph (1)(c)(i) or (ii) is not a regulated Australian vessel if a declaration under section 19 is in force for the vessel.
(4) A vessel in the course of construction is a regulated Australian vessel if the vessel is, after completion, for use as a vessel referred to in subparagraph (1)(c)(i) or subsection (2).
For the purposes of subsection (4), a vessel that has been launched, but has not been completed and delivered, is taken to be a vessel in the course of construction.

section.heading: Definition of overseas voyage

content.p: (1) A vessel’s voyage is an overseas voyage if in the course of the voyage the vessel is present in waters outside the outer limits of the exclusive economic zone of Australia.
(2) Despite subsection (1), a vessel’s voyage is not an overseas voyage if:
the voyage commences from a port in Queensland and ends at the same port or another port in Queensland; and
as an incidental part of its voyage, the vessel is present in waters that are outside the outer limits of the exclusive economic zone of Australia but within the Protected Zone; and
the vessel is not otherwise present in waters that are outside the outer limits of the exclusive economic zone of Australia.

(3) Despite subsection (1), a vessel’s voyage is not an overseas voyage if the presence of the vessel in waters outside the outer limits of the exclusive economic zone of Australia is because of stress of weather, saving life at sea or other unavoidable cause.

section.heading: Definition of Australian Border Force vessel

content.p: (1) A vessel is an Australian Border Force vessel if it is:
(a) used or for use for the purposes of the Australian Border Force (within the meaning of the Australian Border Force Act 2015); and
declared by AMSA by written instrument under subsection (2) to be an Australian Border Force vessel.
AMSA may make a declaration that a vessel, or vessel included in a class of vessels, is an Australian Border Force vessel.
A declaration made under subsection (2) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Definition of special purpose vessel

content.p: A vessel is a special purpose vessel if it is:
a vessel that is used or for use for a purpose specified in the regulations; and
specified by the regulations to be a special purpose vessel for the purposes of this section.

section.heading: AMSA may declare that a vessel is not a regulated Australian vessel

content.p: AMSA may, by written instrument, make a declaration that a vessel, or vessel included in a class of vessels, is not a regulated Australian vessel.
AMSA may make the declaration if AMSA is satisfied of such matters as are prescribed by the regulations.
A declaration made under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Definition of vessel’s length overall

content.p: (1) Subject to subsection (2), the length overall of a vessel is 110% of the length as shown on the vessel’s load line certification.
(2) If the length overall of a vessel cannot be worked out under subsection (1), the length overall is taken to be the distance between:
a vertical line passing through a point that is the foremost part of the bow; and
a vertical line passing through a point that is the aftermost part of the stern.

section.heading: Definition of navigates without a licensed pilot

content.p: (1) Subject to subsection (2), a vessel navigates without a licensed pilot if the vessel does not have a licensed pilot on board to assist the master in navigating it.
If:
apart from this subsection, a vessel navigates without a licensed pilot; and
the vessel is being towed by another vessel that is navigating with a licensed pilot;
the vessel under tow is to be treated as if it had a licensed pilot on board to assist the master in navigating it.

section.heading: Definition of taken to sea

content.p: (1) A vessel is taken to sea if the vessel:
goes to sea, plies, runs or proceeds on a voyage; or
has been got underway for the purpose of going to sea, plying, running or proceeding on a voyage.

Despite subsection (1), a vessel is not taken to sea merely because the vessel has been got underway for the purpose of moving it from one berth or place in a port to another berth or place in the port.

section.heading: Definition of seaworthy

content.p: A vessel is seaworthy if, and only if:

it is in a fit state as to the condition of hull and equipment, boilers (if any) and machinery, the stowage of ballast or cargo, the number and qualifications of seafarers, and in every other respect, to:
encounter the ordinary perils of the voyage undertaken; and
not pose a threat to the environment; and
it is not overloaded; and
the living and working conditions on board the vessel do not pose a threat to the health, safety or welfare of the vessel’s seafarers.
Note: An unseaworthy vessel can be detained under section 248.

section.heading: Definition of substandard

content.p: A vessel to which the Safety Convention, the Load Lines Convention, the Prevention of Pollution Convention or the Maritime Labour Convention applies is substandard, in relation to the condition of the vessel or its equipment in respect of a particular voyage or operation of the vessel, if:
a certificate required by the Convention concerned for the proposed voyage or operation is not in force; or
both:
one or more certificates required by the Convention concerned for the proposed voyage or operation are in force; and
the condition of the vessel or its equipment does not correspond substantially with the particulars of the certificate or certificates.
Note: A substandard vessel can be detained under section 248.

section.heading: Opting in to coverage—vessel declared to be a regulated Australian vessel

content.p: (1) The owner, or any of the owners, of a vessel may apply to AMSA for a declaration (an opt-in declaration) that the vessel is a regulated Australian vessel.
AMSA must, by written instrument, make an opt-in declaration for a vessel if AMSA is satisfied:
(a) that the vessel is registered under the Shipping Registration Act 1981; and
that the vessel is seaworthy; and
that the vessel is not substandard (if applicable); and
of such other matters (if any) as are prescribed by the regulations.
AMSA must make a decision on an application under subsection (1) within 30 days of the making of the application.
An opt-in declaration is not a legislative instrument.
AMSA must not make an opt-in declaration other than as mentioned in subsection (2).

section.heading: Revocation and variation of opt-in declarations

content.p: An opt-in declaration for a vessel ceases to be in force, unless sooner revoked:
at the end of the period, if any, specified in the declaration; or
when the vessel ceases to have Australian nationality.
AMSA must revoke an opt-in declaration for a vessel if AMSA is requested to do so by the owner, or any of the owners, of the vessel and is satisfied of the matters prescribed by the regulations.
AMSA may vary an opt-in declaration for a vessel if:
AMSA is satisfied that the name or any other details of the vessel have been changed since the making of the declaration; and
AMSA is satisfied that it is appropriate to vary, rather than revoke, the declaration.
AMSA may revoke an opt-in declaration for a vessel if:
AMSA is satisfied that the vessel no longer exists or has been lost; or
AMSA is satisfied that the name or any other details of the vessel have been changed since the making of the declaration and that it is appropriate to revoke, rather than vary, the declaration; or
AMSA is no longer satisfied as mentioned in subsection 25(2) in relation to the vessel.

section.heading: Simplified outline of this Chapter

content.p: This Chapter deals with matters relating to seafarers.
Part 2 deals with seafarer certificates.
Part 3 provides for the issue of maritime labour certificates for regulated Australian vessels.
Part 4 deals with the manning of regulated Australian vessels and the engagement of seafarers.
Part 5 deals with the health, accommodation and welfare of seafarers of regulated Australian vessels and foreign vessels.
Part 6 provides for alcohol and drug testing of seafarers of regulated Australian vessels and foreign vessels.
Part 7 contains miscellaneous provisions that relate to seafarers of regulated Australian vessels and foreign vessels.

division.heading: Regulations relating to seafarer certificates

section.heading: Regulations relating to seafarer certificates

content.p: The regulations may make provision in relation to seafarer certificates.
Note: Part 4 of Chapter 9 contains general provisions that apply to regulations about certificates.
Without limiting subsection (1), the regulations may give effect to the STCW Convention.

section.heading: Particular matters that may be prescribed by regulations

content.p: The regulations may prescribe different classes of seafarer certificates and may require that an individual hold a seafarer certificate of a particular kind in order to undertake particular duties, or perform particular functions, as a seafarer.
The regulations may prescribe criteria relating to the following in relation to seafarer certificates:
proficiencies, competencies and standards;
qualifications;
experience;
minimum age;
character;
health;
nationality, citizenship or residence.
The regulations may make provision in relation to the following:
the manner in which the attainment of proficiencies, competencies and standards is to be evidenced;
the instruction, training and examination of seafarers, including:
the gaining of sea service and other experience; and
the conduct of examinations, the conditions for admission to examinations and the appointment and remuneration of examiners;

the recognition of certificates and other documents granted or issued to or in respect of masters, officers and seafarers under the Marine Safety (Domestic Commercial Vessel) National Law of the Commonwealth or a law of a State, a Territory or a foreign country;
conditions to which seafarer certificates are subject.
This section does not limit section 28.

division.heading: Issue of seafarer certificates

section.heading: Persons may apply for a seafarer certificate

content.p: An individual may apply to AMSA for a seafarer certificate of a kind specified in the regulations.
The application must be in accordance with the regulations.

section.heading: Issue of seafarer certificate

content.p: AMSA may issue a seafarer certificate to a person if:
the person has made an application for the certificate under section 30; and
AMSA is satisfied that the criteria prescribed by the regulations are met in relation to the issue of the certificate.
A seafarer certificate is subject to:
the conditions (if any) prescribed by the regulations; and
the conditions (if any) imposed by AMSA.

section.heading: AMSA may vary seafarer certificate

content.p: AMSA may vary a seafarer certificate if AMSA is satisfied that the criteria prescribed by the regulations are met in relation to the variation of the certificate.
Without limiting subsection (1), AMSA may vary a seafarer certificate to impose, vary or remove a condition on the certificate.

section.heading: Revocation of seafarer certificate

content.p: AMSA may revoke a seafarer certificate if AMSA is satisfied that the criteria prescribed by the regulations are met in relation to the revocation of the certificate.

division.heading: Offences and civil penalties relating to seafarer certificates

section.heading: False representations about seafarer certificates

content.p: A person must not represent that he or she holds a seafarer certificate of a particular kind if the representation is false.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 5 years or 300 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 3,000 penalty units.

section.heading: Person performing duties or functions without a seafarer certificate

content.p: A person must not perform duties or functions in relation to a regulated Australian vessel if:
the regulations require the person to hold a particular seafarer certificate in order to perform those duties or functions; and
the person does not hold such a seafarer certificate.
Subsection (1) does not apply to the performance of duties or functions in exceptional circumstances.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 5 years or 300 penalty units, or both.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in subsection (2) (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 3,000 penalty units.
A person who wishes to rely on subsection (2) in proceedings for a civil penalty order bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in that subsection.

section.heading: Master causing etc. performance of duties or functions without a seafarer certificate

content.p: The master of a regulated Australian vessel must not cause or permit another person to perform duties or functions in relation to the vessel if:
the regulations require the other person to hold a particular seafarer certificate in order to perform those duties or functions; and
the other person does not hold such a seafarer certificate.
Subsection (1) does not apply to the performance of duties or functions in exceptional circumstances.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 5 years or 300 penalty units, or both.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in subsection (2) (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 3,000 penalty units.
A person who wishes to rely on subsection (2) in proceedings for a civil penalty order bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in that subsection.

section.heading: Breach of a condition of a seafarer certificate

content.p: A person must not breach a condition of a seafarer certificate held by the person.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 12 months or 60 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.

section.heading: Master causing etc. breach of a condition of a seafarer certificate

content.p: The master of a regulated Australian vessel must not cause or permit another person to breach a condition of a seafarer certificate held by the other person.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 12 months or 60 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.

section.heading: Failing to produce seafarer certificate

content.p: The holder of a seafarer certificate must ensure that the certificate is made available at all reasonable times for examination on request by any of the following:
AMSA;
an inspector;
an officer of Customs.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 12 months or 60 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.

section.heading: AMSA may require delivery of revoked certificates

content.p: If a seafarer certificate is revoked, AMSA may require the certificate to be delivered to AMSA in accordance with the regulations.

division.heading: Vessels to which this Part applies

section.heading: Vessels to which this Part applies

content.p: This Part applies to regulated Australian vessels.

division.heading: Regulations relating to maritime labour certificates

section.heading: Regulations relating to maritime labour certificates

content.p: The regulations may make provision in relation to maritime labour certificates.
Note: Part 4 of Chapter 9 contains general provisions that apply to regulations about certificates.

The regulations may provide that vessels included in a particular class are required to have maritime labour certificates of specified kinds, either generally or in specified circumstances, including certificates relating to the working and living conditions of the vessel’s seafarers.

division.heading: Issue of maritime labour certificates

section.heading: Persons may apply for a maritime labour certificate

content.p: A person may apply to an issuing body for a maritime labour certificate of a kind specified in the regulations for a vessel.
The application must be in accordance with the regulations.

section.heading: Issue of maritime labour certificate

content.p: An issuing body may issue a maritime labour certificate for a vessel if:
an application for the certificate has been made under section 43; and
the issuing body is satisfied that the criteria prescribed by the regulations are met in relation to the issue of the certificate.
A maritime labour certificate is subject to:
the conditions (if any) prescribed by the regulations; and
the conditions (if any) imposed by the issuing body.

section.heading: Issuing body may vary maritime labour certificate

content.p: An issuing body may vary a maritime labour certificate if the issuing body is satisfied that the criteria prescribed by the regulations are met in relation to the variation of the certificate.
Without limiting subsection (1), an issuing body may vary a maritime labour certificate to impose, vary or remove a condition on the certificate.

section.heading: Revocation of maritime labour certificate

content.p: An issuing body may revoke a maritime labour certificate if the issuing body is satisfied that the criteria prescribed by the regulations are met in relation to the revocation of the certificate.

division.heading: Offences and civil penalties relating to taking a vessel to sea without a maritime labour certificate

section.heading: Taking a regulated Australian vessel to sea without maritime labour certificate—owner

content.p: The owner of a regulated Australian vessel must not take the vessel to sea, or cause or permit another person to take the vessel to sea, if:
the vessel is required by the regulations to have a maritime labour certificate of a specified kind; and
a maritime labour certificate of that kind is not in force for the vessel.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 12 months or 60 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.

section.heading: Taking a regulated Australian vessel to sea without maritime labour certificates—master

content.p: The master of a regulated Australian vessel must not take the vessel to sea, or cause or permit another person to take the vessel to sea, if:
the vessel is required by the regulations to have a maritime labour certificate of a specified kind; and
a maritime labour certificate of that kind is not in force for the vessel.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for12 months or 60 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.

section.heading: Obligation to notify alterations of regulated Australian vessels that relate to maritime labour certificates

content.p: A person contravenes this subsection if:
the person is the owner or master of a regulated Australian vessel; and
the vessel is altered in such a way as to affect the maritime labour certificates that vessel is required to have; and
AMSA, and each issuing body that has issued a maritime labour certificate for the vessel, are not informed of the alterations within the period prescribed by the regulations.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 12 months or 60 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.

division.heading: Vessels to which this Part applies

section.heading: Vessels to which this Part applies

content.p: This Part applies to regulated Australian vessels.

division.heading: Manning of vessels

section.heading: Minimum complement of seafarers on vessels

content.p: AMSA may determine in writing that a vessel, or a vessel included in a class of vessels, must carry:
a master who holds a specified seafarer certificate; and
not less than:
a specified number of officers who hold specified seafarer certificates; and
a specified number of seafarers who hold specified seafarer certificates.
AMSA must have regard to any matters prescribed by the regulations in making a determination under subsection (1).

A determination under subsection (1) may require a vessel, or a vessel included in a class of vessels, to carry a master who holds a specified seafarer certificate and to carry a different complement of seafarers:
for different voyages; or
for the carriage of different cargoes; or
for the performance (whether in port or at sea) of different operations done by, or in relation to, the vessel; or
according to whether the vessel is in port or at sea.
A determination under subsection (1) may specify conditions to which the determination is subject.
More than one determination under subsection (1) may apply in relation to a vessel.
A determination made under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Operating a vessel other than in accordance with determination

content.p: The master of a vessel must not operate the vessel, or cause or permit another person to operate the vessel, if:
a determination under section 51 is in force for the vessel; and
the operation of the vessel is not in accordance with the determination.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 5 years or 300 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 3,000 penalty units.

section.heading: Owner or master to give details of complement of vessel’s seafarers

content.p: The owner or master of a vessel must, at such times as are required by AMSA, give to a person prescribed by the regulations such details of, and such details of changes in, the complement of the vessel’s seafarers as the regulations require the owner or the master to give.
Strict liability offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 100 penalty units.

division.heading: Engagement of seafarers, etc.

section.heading: Work agreements

content.p: The master of a vessel must not take the vessel to sea, or cause or permit another person to take the vessel to sea, if:
a seafarer is on board the vessel; and
when the vessel is taken to sea, a work agreement that complies with the regulations made for the purposes of subsection (5) is not in force in relation to the seafarer.
The owner of a vessel must not take the vessel to sea, or cause or permit another person to take the vessel to sea, if:
a seafarer is on board the vessel; and
when the vessel is taken to sea, a work agreement that complies with the regulations made for the purposes of subsection (5) is not in force in relation to the seafarer.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1) or (2).
Penalty: 30 penalty units.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1) or (2).
Civil penalty: 300 penalty units.
Regulations
The regulations may prescribe matters relating to work agreements including, but not limited to, the following:
the content and form of work agreements;
the right of a seafarer to review, and seek advice on, a work agreement before signing it;
the process for signing work agreements;

the information or documents that must be given to, or made available to, seafarers in relation to work agreements and the manner in which such information or documents must be given or made available;
the termination of work agreements;
keeping records of work agreements and retaining such records;
the home port of seafarers.

section.heading: Owner to make available information about conditions of employment

content.p: The regulations may prescribe:
information, in relation to the conditions of employment of seafarers, that the owner of a vessel is required to make available to the vessel’s seafarers; and
the manner and form (including electronic form) in which the prescribed information is required to be made available.
The owner of a vessel must not contravene a requirement of the regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1).
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (2).
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (2).
Civil penalty: 100 penalty units.

section.heading: Offences and civil penalties relating to content of work agreements

content.p: A person must not:
fraudulently alter a work agreement; or
make a false entry in a work agreement; or
give a false copy of a work agreement to another person.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 12 months or 60 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.

section.heading: Regulations about records of service

content.p: The regulations may make provision in relation to keeping, retaining and producing records of service of seafarers.

section.heading: Regulations about hours of work and rest

content.p: The regulations may make provision in relation to the hours of work, and hours of rest, of seafarers.

section.heading: Regulations about payment of wages

content.p: The regulations may make provision in relation to the payment of wages to seafarers.
Without limiting subsection (1), the regulations may make provision in relation to the following:
the frequency of making payments to seafarers;
the method of making payments to seafarers;
permitted deductions from payments to seafarers;
pay slips, including the information relating to exchange rates that must be included in any pay slip given to a seafarer;
the payment of part or all of the wages of a seafarer, with the seafarer’s consent, to a person other than the seafarer;
the charges that may be imposed for making payments in accordance with paragraph (e);
the entitlement to wages of a seafarer left at a port because he or she is ill or injured.
The regulations must not provide for the quantum or amount of wages payable to seafarers.

division.heading: Vessels to which this Part applies

section.heading: Vessels to which this Part applies

content.p: This Part applies to:
regulated Australian vessels; and
foreign vessels.

division.heading: Provisions

section.heading: Regulations about provision of food and water

content.p: The regulations may make provision in relation to the provision of food and drinking water on board vessels.
Without limiting subsection (1), the regulations may make provision in relation to the following:
the quantity and quality of food and drinking water to be carried and made available on board vessels;
mechanisms for making and dealing with complaints about the quantity and quality of food and drinking water.

section.heading: Free provisions

content.p: The owner of a vessel must provide or ensure the provision of free provisions to the vessel’s seafarers.
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 10 penalty units.

section.heading: Provisions adequate for voyage

content.p: The master of a vessel must not take the vessel to sea, or cause or permit the vessel to be taken to sea, unless the vessel is carrying:
drinking water of suitable quality and quantity; and
food of suitable quality, quantity, nutritive value and variety;
having regard to the nature and duration of the voyage and the number, and cultural and religious backgrounds, of the vessel’s seafarers.
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 10 penalty units.

section.heading: Adequate food catering facilities to be provided

content.p: The owner of a vessel must not take the vessel to sea, or cause or permit the vessel to be taken to sea, unless the vessel has catering facilities that are arranged and equipped so as to enable proper meals to be served to the vessel’s seafarers.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 100 penalty units.

division.heading: Health

section.heading: Regulations about health

content.p: The regulations may make provision in relation to the health of seafarers.
Without limiting subsection (1), the regulations may make provision in relation to the following:
the appointment of a person as a medical inspector;
fees payable for services performed by medical inspectors;
the medical examination of seafarers and people proposing to become seafarers, including requirements for:
periodic medical examinations; and
medical examinations on the request of AMSA;
reporting requirements relating to medical examinations;
issuing of certificates of fitness to seafarers and people proposing to become seafarers;
requiring seafarers to hold specified certificates of fitness;
prohibiting the employment or engagement of a person as a seafarer unless the person holds specified certificates of fitness;
medicines, medical and surgical stores and appliances and antiscorbutics;
instructions for dispensing and using medicines, medical and surgical stores and appliances and antiscorbutics;
the inspection of medicines, medical and surgical stores and appliances, antiscorbutics and other things required to be carried on board vessels.

section.heading: Medicines etc. must be carried on vessels—owner

content.p: The owner of a vessel must not take the vessel to sea, or cause or permit the vessel to be taken to sea, unless the vessel is provided, in accordance with the regulations, with:
medicines, medical and surgical stores and appliances and antiscorbutics; and
instructions for dispensing and using medicines, medical and surgical stores and appliances and antiscorbutics.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 100 penalty units.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 1,000 penalty units.

section.heading: Medicines etc. must be carried on vessels—master

content.p: The master of a vessel must not take the vessel to sea, or cause or permit the vessel to be taken to sea, unless the vessel is provided, in accordance with the regulations, with:
medicines, medical and surgical stores and appliances and antiscorbutics; and
instructions for dispensing and using medicines, medical and surgical stores and appliances and antiscorbutics.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 100 penalty units.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 1000 penalty units.

section.heading: Owner liable for medical attendance etc.

content.p: This section applies if a seafarer who is not at his or her home port:
is hurt or injured or contracts a disease; or
suffers from any illness that is not due to an intentional act or default, or to misbehaviour, on the part of the seafarer; or
requires essential dental care.
Expenses for the following are to be paid by the owner of the seafarer’s vessel:
providing the necessary surgical and medical advice and attendance, and medicine, until the seafarer is cured, dies or arrives at that port;
the maintenance of the seafarer until he or she is cured, dies or arrives at that port;
the conveyance of the seafarer to that port;

if the seafarer dies before arriving at that port—his or her burial or, if the seafarer’s body is conveyed to that port at the request of a member of his or her family, the conveyance of the seafarer’s body to that port.

section.heading: Owner liable where certain seafarers removed from vessel etc.

content.p: This section applies if:
a seafarer is suffering from a disease or illness or requires essential dental care; and
the seafarer is temporarily removed from the seafarer’s vessel for the purpose of preventing infection or otherwise for the convenience of the vessel.
Expenses for the following are to be paid by the owner of the vessel:
the removal of the seafarer from, and the seafarer’s return to, the vessel;
providing the necessary surgical and medical advice and attendance, essential dental care and medicine, while the seafarer is away from the vessel;
the maintenance of the seafarer while he or she is away from the vessel.

section.heading: Owner liable for medical attendance etc. on board vessel

content.p: Expenses for all medicine, surgical and medical advice and attendance, and essential dental care, given to a seafarer while the seafarer is on board a vessel must be paid by the owner of the vessel.

section.heading: Other expenses to be paid by seafarer

content.p: Any reasonable expenses incurred by the owner of a vessel in respect of the illness or burial of a seafarer that are not expenses required to be paid by the owner of the seafarer’s vessel under section 68, 69 or 70 may be recovered from the seafarer.

section.heading: Medical practitioners and first-aid attendants—owner

content.p: The owner of a vessel that has 100 or more persons on board must ensure that a qualified medical practitioner is carried, as part of the vessel’s complement, if the vessel is:
proceeding on an overseas voyage; or
on a passage between 2 consecutive ports which exceeds the distance prescribed by the regulations.

The owner of a vessel that has more than 10 but fewer than 100 persons on board must cause to be carried as part of its complement a person qualified, in accordance with the regulations, to render first aid, if the vessel is:
proceeding on an overseas voyage; or
on a passage between 2 consecutive ports which exceeds the distance prescribed by the regulations;
unless the vessel is carrying a qualified medical practitioner as part of its complement.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1) or (2).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 12 months or 60 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1) or (2).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.

section.heading: Medical practitioners and first-aid attendants—master

content.p: The master of a vessel that has 100 or more persons on board must ensure that a qualified medical practitioner is carried, as part of the vessel’s complement, if the vessel is:
proceeding on an overseas voyage; or
on a passage between 2 consecutive ports which exceeds the distance prescribed by the regulations.

The master of a vessel that has more than 10 but fewer than 100 persons on board must cause to be carried as part of its complement a person prescribed by the regulations as qualified to render first aid if the vessel is:
proceeding on an overseas voyage; or
on a passage between 2 consecutive ports which exceeds the distance prescribed by the regulations;
unless the vessel is carrying a qualified medical practitioner as part of its complement.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1) or (2).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 12 months or 60 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1) or (2).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.

division.heading: Accommodation, etc.

section.heading: Regulations relating to accommodation, etc.

content.p: The regulations may make provision in relation to accommodation to be provided for seafarers on vessels.
Without limiting subsection (1), the regulations may make provision in relation to the following:
the minimum amount of space to be provided for each seafarer;
the maximum number of seafarers to be accommodated in a specified part of a vessel;
the part of a vessel in which the whole or a part of the accommodation is to be provided;
the requirements for the construction, furnishing and equipment of the accommodation, including heating, lighting and ventilation;
the maximum levels of noise, vibration and other ambient factors;
the maintenance and repair of the accommodation;
the prohibition or restriction of the use of accommodation for a purpose other than that specified;
the provision of hot and cold fresh water;
the provision of bedding, mess utensils, towels and toiletries;
the submission of plans and specifications relating to the provision or alteration of accommodation.
Regulations may make provision in relation to the following:
the provision of ventilation of machinery and boiler spaces;
the provision of wheelhouses.

section.heading: Vessels not to go to sea without required accommodation

content.p: The owner of a vessel must not take the vessel to sea, or cause or permit the vessel to be taken to sea, if the vessel does not comply with the accommodation prescribed by the regulations made for the purposes of subsection 74(1).
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 100 penalty units.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 1,000 penalty units.

division.heading: Repatriation and protection

section.heading: Regulations relating to repatriation

content.p: The regulations may make provision in relation to the repatriation of seafarers at no cost to the seafarer.
Without limiting subsection (1), the regulations may make provision for or in relation to the following:
the circumstances in which a seafarer is entitled to be repatriated, including in the following circumstances:
expiry or termination of the seafarer’s work agreement;
inability to carry out the seafarer’s duties;
injury or illness of the seafarer;
transfer, sale or wreck of the seafarer’s vessel;
the liability for the costs of repatriation and recovery of costs;
the mode of transport of repatriation;
the destination to which the seafarer is repatriated.

section.heading: Regulations relating to complaints etc. about employment

content.p: The regulations may make provision in relation to complaints and legal proceedings relating to a seafarer’s employment, including in relation to:
how such complaints are to be handled; and
leave to go to shore in relation to such complaints or legal proceedings.

division.heading: Alcohol and drug testing of seafarers and pilots

section.heading: Seafarer or licensed pilot may be required to undergo alcohol test

content.p: AMSA may require a seafarer or a licensed pilot on board a regulated Australian vessel or a foreign vessel to undergo a test of a kind prescribed by the regulations for the purpose of determining the level of alcohol in the blood of the seafarer or pilot.

section.heading: Seafarer or licensed pilot may be required to undergo drug tests etc.

content.p: AMSA may require a seafarer or a licensed pilot on board a regulated Australian vessel or a foreign vessel to undergo a test of a kind prescribed by the regulations for the purpose of determining the presence of a drug in the blood of the seafarer or pilot.

section.heading: Limitation on exercise of powers in relation to foreign vessels

content.p: AMSA must not exercise a power under section 78 or 79 in relation to a seafarer of a foreign vessel, or a pilot on board a foreign vessel, unless the vessel is:
in an Australian port; or
entering or leaving an Australian port; or
in the internal waters of Australia; or
in the territorial sea of Australia, other than in the course of innocent passage.

section.heading: Refusal to undergo alcohol or drug test

content.p: A person contravenes this subsection if:
the person has been required to undergo an alcohol test or a drug test; and
the person fails to undergo the test.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 60 penalty units.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.

section.heading: Information to be provided after test

content.p: As soon as practicable after a seafarer or a licensed pilot has undergone an alcohol test or a drug test, the person who conducted the test must give the seafarer or pilot a written statement specifying:
the test result; and
the date and time of the test.

division.heading: Offences and civil penalties relating to alcohol and drugs

section.heading: Impairment of person’s capacity to carry out duties as seafarer or pilot

content.p: A person contravenes this subsection if:
the person is a seafarer or a licensed pilot on board a regulated Australian vessel or a foreign vessel; and
the person is under the influence of alcohol or any other drug (whether medicinal or otherwise) to such an extent that his or her capacity to carry out the duties of a seafarer or pilot is impaired.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 60 penalty units.

section.heading: Unacceptable blood alcohol level—seafarers and pilots

content.p: A person contravenes this subsection if:
the person is a seafarer or a licensed pilot on board a regulated Australian vessel or a foreign vessel; and
the blood alcohol level of the person equals or exceeds the blood alcohol level prescribed by the regulations.
Strict liability offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
Penalty: 60 penalty units.

section.heading: Drugs prescribed by the regulations: seafarers and pilots

content.p: A person contravenes this subsection if:
the person is a seafarer or a licensed pilot on board a regulated Australian vessel or a foreign vessel; and
a drug prescribed by the regulations is present in the blood of the person.
Strict liability offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
Penalty: 60 penalty units.

section.heading: Permitting or requiring performance of duties by impaired person

content.p: A person contravenes this subsection if:
the person is the owner or master of a regulated Australian vessel or a foreign vessel; and
the person permits or requires a seafarer or pilot to undertake or to continue duty on board the vessel; and
the person knows that the capacity of the seafarer or pilot to perform those duties is impaired by the influence of alcohol or any other drug (whether medicinal or otherwise).
Strict liability offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
Penalty: 60 penalty units.

division.heading: Regulations and other matters

section.heading: Regulations relating to alcohol and drug tests

content.p: The regulations may make provision in relation to the following:
the authorisation of persons:
to conduct alcohol tests and drug tests; and
to operate devices equipment for that purpose;
the conduct of alcohol tests and drug tests, including random tests and tests with notice;
the devices used in conducting alcohol tests and drug tests, including the calibration, inspection and testing of those devices;
the approval of persons to conduct analyses in connection with such tests;
the procedure for the handling and analysis of samples;
the confidentiality of test results;
the storage and destruction of samples.

section.heading: Evidentiary certificates

content.p: A person who conducts an alcohol test or a drug test may issue a certificate stating:
that he or she conducted an alcohol test or a drug test of a person named in the certificate; and
the steps taken in conducting the test; and
that the person was given a statement in writing under section 82.
In any proceedings relating to this Part, a certificate under this section is prima-facie evidence of the matters in the certificate.
A document purporting to be a certificate under this section must, unless the contrary is proved, be taken to be such a certificate and to have been properly issued.

A certificate must not be admitted in evidence in proceedings in relation to an offence or a civil penalty unless the person against whom the proceedings were instituted has, at least 14 days before the certificate is sought to be admitted, been given:
a copy of the certificate; and
reasonable notice of the intention to produce the certificate as evidence in the proceedings.

part.heading: General matters relating to seafarers of regulated Australian vessels and foreign vessels

section.heading: Exemption from serving on jury

content.p: A seafarer of a regulated Australian vessel or a foreign vessel is exempt from serving as a juror under the law of the Commonwealth or of a State or Territory.

section.heading: Seafarer not to be wrongfully left behind

content.p: A person must not:
force onshore and leave behind at a place (whether within Australia or outside Australia) a seafarer of a regulated Australian vessel or a foreign vessel; or
otherwise cause such a seafarer to be left behind at such a place, either onshore or at sea.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 12 months or 60 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.

section.heading: Regulations may make provision in relation to property of deceased seafarers

content.p: The regulations may make provision in relation to dealing with the property of deceased seafarers of regulated Australian vessels and foreign vessels.

section.heading: Expenses of returning foreign seafarers left behind

content.p: If:
a seafarer of a foreign vessel is left behind at an Australian port or dies in Australia; and
the Commonwealth incurs expense in sending the seafarer, the seafarer’s body or any property of the seafarer outside Australia;

the Commonwealth may recover the amount of those expenses from the owner, agent or master of the vessel in an eligible court as a debt due and payable by the owner, agent or master to the Commonwealth.

section.heading: Owner of vessel not entitled to limit liability in respect of certain claims

content.p: The owner of a regulated Australian vessel or a foreign vessel is not entitled to limit his, her or its liability in respect of any claim described in paragraph 1(a) of Article 2 of the Limitation of Liability for Maritime Claims Convention made by:
a servant (within the meaning of the Convention) of the owner whose duties are connected with the vessel; or
any heir or dependant of the servant or any other person who is, within the meaning of paragraph (e) of Article 3 of the Convention, a person entitled to make such a claim.

section.heading: Employment of seafarers in loading and unloading

content.p: A person must not employ a seafarer at an Australian port in handling cargo in connection with the loading or unloading of a regulated Australian vessel or a foreign vessel:
if sufficient shore labour is available; or
if sufficient shore labour is not available—other than in accordance with any requirements prescribed by the regulations.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 100 penalty units.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 1,000 penalty units.

section.heading: Copy of this Act to be kept on regulated Australian vessels

content.p: The master of a regulated Australian vessel must provide the vessel’s seafarers with access (whether electronic or otherwise), at all reasonable times, to a copy of this Act.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 5 penalty units.
Reference to Act does not include regulations, etc.
In subsection (1), a reference to this Act does not include regulations or other legislative instruments under this Act.
Regulations may require instruments to be accessible

The regulations may require the master of a regulated Australian vessel to provide the vessel’s seafarers with access (whether electronic or otherwise), at all reasonable times, to a copy of specified regulations or other legislative instruments made under this Act.

section.heading: Simplified outline of this Chapter

content.p: This Chapter deals with the safety of regulated Australian vessels and foreign vessels.
Part 2 deals with safety certificates for regulated Australian vessels and documentation for foreign vessels. It provides for offences and civil penalties that apply in relation to:
taking regulated Australian vessels to sea without safety certificates; and
taking foreign vessels to sea without appropriate documents.
Part 3 deals with offences and civil penalties for taking to sea an unseaworthy regulated Australian vessel or foreign vessel.
Part 4 deals with passenger and cargo operations of regulated Australian vessels and foreign vessels, including in relation to:
overloading (Division 3); and
loading (Subdivision A of Division 4); and
dangerous goods (Subdivision B of Division 4).
Part 5 deals with the carrying out of musters and drills on regulated Australian vessels, foreign vessels, domestic commercial vessels and recreational vessels.

division.heading: Vessels to which this Part applies

section.heading: Vessels to which this Part applies

content.p: This Part applies to:
regulated Australian vessels; and
foreign vessels.

division.heading: Regulations relating to safety certificates

section.heading: Regulations relating to safety certificates

content.p: The regulations may make provision in relation to safety certificates.
Note: Part 4 of Chapter 9 contains general provisions that apply to regulations about certificates.
Without limiting subsection (1), the regulations may make provision in relation to giving effect to the following:
the Safety Convention;
the Load Lines Convention.

The regulations may provide that vessels included in a particular class are required to have safety certificates of specified kinds, either generally or in specified circumstances, including certificates relating to the following matters:
survey;
construction;
machinery and equipment;
other matters relating to the safety of vessels.

division.heading: Issue of safety certificates

section.heading: Persons may apply for a safety certificate

content.p: A person may apply to an issuing body for a safety certificate of a kind specified in the regulations for a regulated Australian vessel.
The application must be in accordance with the regulations.

section.heading: Issue of safety certificate

content.p: An issuing body may issue a safety certificate for a regulated Australian vessel if:
an application for the certificate has been made under section 99; and
the issuing body is satisfied that the criteria prescribed by the regulations in relation to the issue of the certificate are met.
A safety certificate is subject to:
the conditions (if any) prescribed by the regulations; and
the conditions (if any) imposed by the issuing body.

section.heading: Issuing body may vary safety certificate

content.p: An issuing body may vary a safety certificate if the issuing body is satisfied that the criteria prescribed by the regulations in relation to the variation of the certificate are met.
Without limiting subsection (1), an issuing body may vary a safety certificate to impose, vary or remove a condition on the certificate.

section.heading: Revocation of safety certificate

content.p: An issuing body may revoke a safety certificate if the issuing body is satisfied that the criteria prescribed by the regulations in relation to the revocation of the certificate are met.

division.heading: Offences and civil penalties relating to taking a regulated Australian vessel to sea without safety certificates

section.heading: Taking a regulated Australian vessel to sea without safety certificate—owner

content.p: The owner of a regulated Australian vessel must not take the vessel to sea, or cause or permit another person to take the vessel to sea, if:
the vessel is required by the regulations to have a safety certificate of a specified kind; and
such a safety certificate is not in force for the vessel.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 10 years or 600 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 6,000 penalty units.

section.heading: Taking a regulated Australian vessel to sea without safety certificate—master

content.p: The master of a regulated Australian vessel must not take the vessel to sea, or cause or permit another person to take the vessel to sea, if:
the vessel is required by the regulations to have a safety certificate of a specified kind; and
such a safety certificate is not in force for the vessel.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 10 years or 600 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 6,000 penalty units.

section.heading: Obligation to notify alterations of regulated Australian vessels that relate to safety certificates

content.p: A person contravenes this subsection if:
the person is the owner or master of a regulated Australian vessel; and
the vessel is altered so as to affect the safety certificates that vessel is required to have; and
AMSA, and each issuing body that has issued a safety certificate that is in force for the vessel, are not informed of the alterations within the period prescribed by the regulations.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 12 months or 60 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.

division.heading: Offences and civil penalties relating to taking foreign vessels to sea without appropriate documents

section.heading: Taking a foreign vessel to sea without appropriate documents—owner

content.p: The owner of a foreign vessel must not take the vessel to sea, or cause or permit another person to take the vessel to sea, if:
the vessel is required by the regulations to have a certificate of a specified kind and such a certificate is not in force for the vessel; or

if the vessel is not required by the regulations to have a certificate of a specified kind—other documentary evidence attesting that the vessel is seaworthy, issued by or on behalf of the country in which the vessel is or may be registered, is not in force.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 10 years or 600 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 6,000 penalty units.

section.heading: Taking a foreign vessel to sea without appropriate documents—master

content.p: The master of a foreign vessel must not take the vessel to sea, or cause or permit another person to take the vessel to sea, if:
the vessel is required by the regulations to have a certificate of a specified kind and such a certificate is not in force for the vessel; or

if the vessel is not required by the regulations to have a certificate of a specified kind—other documentary evidence attesting that the vessel is seaworthy, issued by or on behalf of the country in which the vessel is registered, is not in force.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 10 years or 600 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 6,000 penalty units.

section.heading: Vessels to which this Part applies

content.p: This Part applies to:
regulated Australian vessels; and
foreign vessels.

section.heading: Taking unseaworthy vessel to sea—owner

content.p: The owner of a vessel must not take the vessel to sea, or cause or permit another person to take the vessel to sea, if the vessel is unseaworthy.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 10 years or 600 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 6,000 penalty units.

section.heading: Taking unseaworthy vessel to sea—master

content.p: The master of a vessel must not take the vessel to sea, or cause or permit another person to take the vessel to sea, if the vessel is unseaworthy.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 10 years or 600 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 6,000 penalty units.

part.heading: Passenger and cargo operations, and overloading

division.heading: Vessels to which this Part applies

section.heading: Vessels to which this Part applies

content.p: This Part applies to:
regulated Australian vessels; and
foreign vessels.

division.heading: Regulations relating to passenger and cargo operations

section.heading: Regulations relating to passenger and cargo operations

content.p: Passengers
The regulations may make provision in relation to the carriage of passengers.
Without limiting subsection (1), the regulations may make provision in relation to the following:
equipment;
the number of passengers to be carried;
accommodation;
provisions and water;
medical and surgical stores;
medical inspection;
medical staff and attendants;
hospital accommodation;
sanitary matters;
discipline;
passenger lists.
Without limiting subsection (1), the regulations may make provision in relation to:
the obligations to passengers of the owner and master of a wrecked vessel or a vessel that is unable to proceed on a voyage; and
the landing of passengers at a port other than in accordance with a contract.
Loading of cargo and livestock
The regulations may make provision in relation to the carriage on a vessel of cargo and livestock.
Without limiting subsection (4), the regulations may make provision in relation to the following:
the loading, stowing or carriage of cargo or livestock in vessels;
the unloading of cargo and livestock from vessels;
the giving of notices relating to a matter referred to in paragraph (a) or (b).
Dangerous goods
The regulations may make provision in relation to the carriage of dangerous goods.
Without limiting subsection (6), the regulations may make provision in relation to the following:
the classes of vessels in which dangerous goods may be carried;
the quantities of dangerous goods that may be carried from an Australian port;
the precautions to be observed in connection with loading or unloading dangerous goods at an Australian port;
the conditions as to the packing and stowing of dangerous goods loaded at an Australian port, and the ventilation of holds containing such goods.

division.heading: Regulations relating to overloading

section.heading: Regulations relating to overloading

content.p: The regulations may make provision in relation to the following:
when a vessel is overloaded;
the giving of notices relating to the overloading of a vessel.

division.heading: Offences and civil penalties relating to passenger and cargo operations

content.p: Subdivision A—Loading

section.heading: Proper precautions in loading a vessel

content.p: A person who is involved in an activity of packing, sending, stowing, loading, unloading, securing or carrying cargo, livestock or ship’s stores on a vessel contravenes this subsection if:
the person does not:
ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, that the activity is carried out in such a way that it does not damage the vessel, risk the safety of a person or damage the environment; and
carry out, or arrange the carrying out of, such procedures as may be necessary for compliance with subparagraph (i); and
in the case of a foreign vessel—when the activity concerned occurs, the vessel is:
in an Australian port; or
entering or leaving an Australian port; or
in the internal waters of Australia; or
in the territorial sea of Australia, other than in the course of innocent passage.

Without limiting subsection (1), an owner of a vessel contravenes that subsection if the owner does not implement and maintain a safety management system that ensures, so far as is reasonably practicable, that an activity referred to in that paragraph is carried out in such a way that it does not damage the vessel, risk the safety of a person or damage the environment.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person:
contravenes subsection (1); and
is reckless as to whether the activity that constitutes the contravention risks damaging the vessel, the safety of a person or damaging the environment.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 5 years or 300 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.
Subdivision B—Dangerous goods

section.heading: Carrying improperly labelled dangerous goods on a vessel

content.p: A person contravenes this subsection if:
the person carries dangerous goods on board, or causes or permits dangerous goods to be placed for carriage on board, a regulated Australian vessel or a foreign vessel; and
the outside of the package containing the goods is not distinctly marked with a correct description of the goods; and
if the vessel is a foreign vessel—at the time when the goods are carried or placed on board the vessel, the vessel is:
in an Australian port; or
entering or leaving an Australian port; or
in the internal waters of Australia; or
in the territorial sea of Australia, other than in the course of innocent passage.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 12 months or 60 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.

section.heading: Requirement to give a description to master or owner of dangerous goods on a vessel

content.p: A person contravenes this subsection if:
the person causes or permits dangerous goods to be placed on board a vessel; and
the person is not the owner or master of the vessel; and

a description in writing of the goods, additional to the description contained in the ordinary shipping documents related to the vessel, is not given to the owner or master of the vessel at or before the time the goods are placed on board the vessel; and
if the vessel is a foreign vessel—at the time when the goods are placed on board the vessel, the vessel is:
in an Australian port; or
entering or leaving an Australian port; or
in the internal waters of Australia; or
in the territorial sea of Australia, other than in the course of innocent passage.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 12 months or 60 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.

section.heading: Carrying etc. dangerous goods under a false description

content.p: A person contravenes this subsection if:
the person carries dangerous goods on board a vessel under a false description, or causes or permits dangerous goods to be carried on board a vessel under a false description; and
if the vessel is a foreign vessel—at the time when the goods are carried, the vessel is:
in an Australian port; or
entering or leaving an Australian port; or
in the internal waters of Australia; or
in the territorial sea of Australia, other than in the course of innocent passage.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 12 months or 60 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.

section.heading: Falsely describing the sender of dangerous goods

content.p: A person contravenes this subsection if:
dangerous goods are or will be carried on a vessel; and
the person describes the sender of the goods:
on the packaging containing the goods; or
on any document relating to the carrying of the goods; and
the description is false or misleading in a material particular.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 12 months or 60 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.

section.heading: Notice of intention to ship

content.p: Before dangerous goods are shipped in a regulated Australian vessel or a foreign vessel, the shipper must give notice of his or her intention, in the manner and to the person prescribed by the regulations, to ship the goods.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 12 months or 60 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.

section.heading: Powers of owner or master as to dangerous goods

content.p: The owner or master of a vessel may:
refuse to carry any dangerous goods; and
open and inspect any package suspected of containing dangerous goods;
and is not to be subject to any liability of any kind for so doing.
Subdivision C—Other offences

section.heading: Obstructing vessel or machinery

content.p: A passenger or other person on board a vessel must not:
obstruct or interfere with any part of the machinery or equipment of the vessel; or
obstruct, hinder or harm a seafarer on board the vessel.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 2 years or 120 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.

section.heading: Certain persons may be refused entry to or asked to leave a vessel

content.p: A person must not:
board a vessel after being refused permission to board by or on behalf of the owner or master; or
remain on board a vessel after being asked to leave the vessel by or on behalf of the owner or master.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 10 penalty units.

section.heading: Power of master etc. to detain

content.p: (1) If the master or other officer of a vessel reasonably believes that a person (the offender) has contravened section 121, the master or officer, or a person asked by the master or officer to assist, may detain the offender without warrant.

A person who detains an offender under subsection (1) must, as soon as practicable after the detention, arrange for the offender, and any property found on the offender, to be delivered to a constable.

division.heading: Vessels to which this Part applies

section.heading: Vessels to which this Part applies

content.p: This Part applies to:
regulated Australian vessels; and
foreign vessels; and
domestic commercial vessels; and
recreational vessels.

division.heading: Regulations relating to musters, drills and tests

section.heading: Regulations relating to musters, drills and tests

content.p: The regulations may make provision in relation to musters, drills, checks of machinery and equipment and other tests.
Without limiting subsection (1), the regulations may make provision in relation to the following:
boat drills, fire drills and collision drills;
safety training and familiarisation;
checks and tests of machinery and equipment;
entries in a vessel’s official logbook of musters, drills and safety training and familiarisation.

division.heading: Offences and civil penalties relating to musters, drills and tests

section.heading: Musters and drills etc. on vessels

content.p: The master of a vessel must ensure:
that musters, drills and safety training and familiarisation are held in accordance with the regulations; and
that entries are made in the vessel’s official logbook, in accordance with the regulations, in relation to musters, drills and safety training and familiarisation.

Without limiting subsection (1), the master of a vessel contravenes that subsection if the master does not implement and maintain a safety management system that ensures that the musters, drills and safety training and familiarisation are held.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 5 years or 300 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 3,000 penalty units.

section.heading: Machinery and equipment checks and tests on vessels

content.p: The master of a regulated Australian vessel or a foreign vessel must ensure:
that checks and tests of the machinery and equipment of the vessel are conducted as required by the regulations; and
that entries are made in the vessel’s official logbook, in accordance with the regulations, in relation to such checks and tests.

Without limiting subsection (1), the master of a vessel contravenes that subsection if the master does not implement and maintain a safety management system that ensures that the checks and tests are carried out, and the entries are made.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 5 years or 300 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 3,000 penalty units.

section.heading: Simplified outline of this Chapter

content.p: This Chapter deals with pollution from vessels.

Part 2 provides for pollution certificates for regulated Australian vessels and certain other Australian vessels. It provides for offences and civil penalty provisions that apply in relation to taking regulated Australian vessels and certain other Australian vessels to sea without pollution certificates.
Part 3 provides for offences and civil penalties for polluting the marine environment.
Part 4 enables directions to be given to foreign vessels in certain circumstances relating to the Prevention of Pollution Convention.

division.heading: Vessels to which this Part applies

section.heading: Vessels to which this Part applies

domestic commercial vessels; and
recreational vessels that have Australian nationality.

division.heading: Regulations relating to pollution certificates

section.heading: Regulations relating to pollution certificates

content.p: The regulations may make provision in relation to pollution certificates.

vessel construction or equipment;
. (b) carriage of noxious liquids or oil;

sewage or garbage;

energy efficiency.

division.heading: Issue of pollution certificates

section.heading: Persons may apply for a pollution certificate

The application must be in accordance with the regulations.

section.heading: Issue of pollution certificate

section.heading: Issuing body may vary pollution certificate

section.heading: Revocation of pollution certificates

section.heading: Taking vessels to sea without pollution certificates—master

content.p: The master of a vessel must not take the vessel to sea, or cause or permit another person to take the vessel to sea, if:
the vessel is required by the regulations to have a pollution certificate of a specified kind; and
a pollution certificate of that kind is not in force for the vessel.

A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).

A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).

section.heading: Obligation to notify alterations of vessels that relate to pollution certificates

content.p: A person contravenes this subsection if:

the vessel is altered so as to affect the pollution certificates the vessel is required to have; and
