Penalty: Imprisonment for 5 years or 300 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 3,000 penalty units.

part.heading: Pollution or damage to the marine environment

division.heading: Vessels to which this Part applies

section.heading: Vessels to which this Part applies

content.p: This Part applies to:
regulated Australian vessels; and
domestic commercial vessels; and
foreign vessels; and
recreational vessels.

section.heading: Geographical application

content.p: This Part applies to a vessel situated in any of the following areas:
waters within the coastal sea of Australia;
waters within the exclusive economic zone of Australia;
waters that are beyond the exclusive economic zone of Australia.
Section 9 does not apply to an offence against Division 2 or 3A or a civil penalty provision in Division 2 or 3A.
The master or owner of a foreign vessel, or a recreational vessel that does not have Australian nationality:
does not commit an offence against Division 2 that relates to the vessel; and
is not liable for a civil penalty for a contravention of a civil penalty provision in Division 2 that relates to the vessel;
unless, at the time when the conduct constituting the alleged offence or contravention occurs, the vessel is:
in an Australian port; or
entering or leaving an Australian port; or
in the internal waters of Australia; or
in the territorial sea of Australia; or
in the exclusive economic zone of Australia; or
an Australian-based foreign Greater Sunrise vessel.

division.heading: Vessels polluting or damaging the Australian marine environment

section.heading: Operating a vessel so as to pollute or damage the Australian marine environment

content.p: The master of a vessel must not operate the vessel in a manner that causes:
pollution to the marine environment in the coastal sea of Australia or the exclusive economic zone of Australia; or
damage to the marine environment in the coastal sea of Australia or the exclusive economic zone of Australia.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 600 penalty units.
Recklessness or negligence is the fault element for:
the manner of operation of the vessel; and
the result mentioned in paragraph (1)(a) or (b) occurring.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty:
for an aggravated contravention—6,000 penalty units; or
in any other case—600 penalty units.

section.heading: Failure to ensure vessel is operated so as not to cause pollution or damage to the Australian marine environment

content.p: The master of a vessel must ensure that the vessel is operated in a manner that does not cause:
pollution to the marine environment in the coastal sea of Australia or the exclusive economic zone of Australia; and
damage to the marine environment in the coastal sea of Australia or the exclusive economic zone of Australia.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 600 penalty units.
Recklessness or negligence is the fault element for:
the operation of the vessel in a manner that causes the result mentioned in paragraph (1)(a) or (b); and
the result mentioned in paragraph (1)(a) or (b) occurring.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty:
for an aggravated contravention—6,000 penalty units; or
in any other case—600 penalty units.

division.heading: Australian vessels polluting or damaging the marine environment outside Australia

section.heading: Operating a vessel so as to pollute or damage the marine environment outside Australia

content.p: The master of a regulated Australian vessel, a domestic commercial vessel, or a recreational vessel that has Australian nationality, must not operate the vessel in a manner that causes:
pollution to the marine environment in seas that are beyond the territorial sea and the exclusive economic zone of Australia; or
damage to the marine environment in seas that are beyond the territorial sea and the exclusive economic zone of Australia.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 600 penalty units.
Recklessness or negligence is the fault element for:
the manner of operation of the vessel; and
the result mentioned in paragraph (1)(a) or (b) occurring.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty:
for an aggravated contravention—6,000 penalty units; or
in any other case—600 penalty units.

section.heading: Failure to ensure vessel is operated so as not to cause pollution or damage to the marine environment outside Australia

content.p: The master of a regulated Australian vessel, a domestic commercial vessel or a recreational vessel that has Australian nationality must ensure that the vessel is operated in a manner that does not cause:
pollution to the marine environment in seas that are beyond the territorial sea and the exclusive economic zone of Australia; or
damage to the marine environment in seas that are beyond the territorial sea and the exclusive economic zone of Australia.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 600 penalty units.
Recklessness or negligence is the fault element for:
the manner of operation of the vessel; and
the result mentioned in paragraph (1)(a) or (b) occurring.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty:
for an aggravated contravention—6,000 penalty units; or
in any other case—600 penalty units.

division.heading: Australian-based foreign Greater sunrise vessels polluting or damaging the marine environment in the Greater Sunrise special regime area

section.heading: Operating an Australian-based foreign Greater Sunrise vessel so as to pollute or damage the marine environment in the Greater Sunrise special regime area

content.p: The master of an Australian-based foreign Greater Sunrise vessel must not operate the vessel in a manner that causes:
pollution to the marine environment in seas that are above the Greater Sunrise special regime area; or
damage to the marine environment in seas that are above the Greater Sunrise special regime area.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 600 penalty units.
Recklessness or negligence is the fault element for:
the manner of operation of the vessel; and
the result mentioned in paragraph (1)(a) or (b) occurring.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty:
for an aggravated contravention—6,000 penalty units; or
in any other case—600 penalty units.

section.heading: Failure to ensure Australian-based foreign Greater Sunrise vessel is operated so as not to cause pollution or damage to the marine environment in the Greater Sunrise special regime area

content.p: The master of an Australian-based foreign Greater Sunrise vessel must ensure that the vessel is operated in a manner that does not cause:
pollution to the marine environment in seas that are above the Greater Sunrise special regime area; or
damage to the marine environment in seas that are above the Greater Sunrise special regime area.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 600 penalty units.
Recklessness or negligence is the fault element for:
the manner of operation of the vessel; and
the result mentioned in paragraph (1)(a) or (b) occurring.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty:
for an aggravated contravention—6,000 penalty units; or
in any other case—600 penalty units.

division.heading: Aggravated contraventions of civil penalty provisions and matters to which eligible court may have regard in determining standard of care etc.

section.heading: Aggravated contraventions of civil penalty provisions

content.p: (1) A contravention of a civil penalty provision of this Part by a person is an aggravated contravention if the person’s act or omission that constituted the contravention:
resulted in serious harm to the marine environment; or
had the potential to cause serious harm to the marine environment.
In determining whether an act or omission has resulted in serious harm to the marine environment, the eligible court may have regard to the following:
the harm;
the size of the affected environment;
the sensitivity of the affected environment;
the significance of the affected environment;
whether the harm is irreversible;
the measures required to remedy the harm.
In determining whether an act or omission had the potential to cause serious harm to the marine environment, the eligible court may have regard to the following:
the potential harm;
the size of the potentially affected environment;
the sensitivity of the potentially affected environment;
the significance of the potentially affected environment;
whether the harm would have been irreversible, had it occurred;
the measures that would have been required to remedy the harm, had it occurred.

If AMSA intends to prove that the person has committed an aggravated contravention, AMSA’s application for a civil penalty order in relation to the contravention must specify the relevant aggravated contravention.
If, in proceedings for a civil penalty order in relation to an aggravated contravention of a provision of this Part, the eligible court:
is not satisfied that the person has committed an aggravated contravention of that provision; and
is satisfied beyond reasonable doubt that the person has contravened that provision;
the eligible court may make a civil penalty order against the person not for the aggravated contravention but for the contravention of that provision.

section.heading: Matters to which eligible court may have regard in determining standard of care and risk

content.p: In determining the standard of care a reasonable person would exercise in operating a vessel and whether there was a risk that a result mentioned in a provision of this Part would happen, the matters to which the eligible court may have regard include the following:
the characteristics of the vessel;
the vessel’s cargo and the risks of pollution or damage to the marine environment if that cargo is released;
the amount of bunker oil on board the vessel and the risk of pollution or damage to the marine environment if that amount of oil is released;
the state of visibility;
the state of the wind, sea and current;
the presence of other vessels in the vicinity;
the presence of navigation hazards in the vicinity;
the rules under the Prevention of Collisions Convention;
operational requirements imposed by law.

part.heading: Directions powers relating to foreign vessels

division.heading: Vessels to which this Part applies

section.heading: Vessels to which this Part applies

content.p: This Part applies to foreign vessels.

division.heading: Directions may be given to vessels

section.heading: Directions in relation to vessels

content.p: If AMSA is satisfied that a vessel is not constructed, equipped or operated in accordance with the Prevention of Pollution Convention (whether or not the vessel is required to be so constructed, equipped or operated), AMSA may give to the master or the owner of a vessel a written direction that requires one or more of the following:
that the vessel not enter or use any port, or a specified port or specified ports, in Australia or the exclusive economic zone of Australia;
that the vessel comply with specified requirements while it:
is approaching, entering, or using any port, or a specified port or specified ports, in Australia or the exclusive economic zone of Australia; or
is in or is leaving any port, or a specified port or specified ports, in Australia or the exclusive economic zone of Australia.
AMSA may exercise its powers under subsection (1) in relation to a vessel only to the extent that AMSA is satisfied that it is necessary or expedient to do so for the protection of the environment.
A direction under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Persons must comply with direction

content.p: A person who is given a direction under section 147 must comply with the direction.
Subsection (1) does not apply if:
the failure to comply with the direction resulted from the need to save life at sea or was due to an emergency involving a threat to a person’s life; or
compliance with the direction was not possible.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 10 years or 600 penalty units, or both.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in subsection (2) (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 6,000 penalty units.
A person who wishes to rely on subsection (2) in proceedings for a civil penalty order bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in that subsection.

section.heading: Geographical application

content.p: Section 9 does not apply to:
an offence against subsection 148(3); or
a contravention of subsection 148(1), so far as it is a civil penalty provision.
The master or owner of a foreign vessel who is given a direction under section 147:
does not commit an offence against subsection 148(3) that relates to the vessel; and
is not liable for a civil penalty for a contravention of subsection 148(1) that relates to the vessel;
unless, at the time when the conduct constituting the alleged offence or contravention occurs, the vessel concerned is:
in an Australian port; or
entering or leaving an Australian port; or
in the internal waters of Australia; or
in the territorial sea of Australia; or
in the exclusive economic zone of Australia; or
an Australian-based foreign Greater Sunrise vessel.

section.heading: Simplified outline of this Chapter

content.p: This Chapter deals with the tonnage of certain vessels.

section.heading: Vessels to which this Chapter applies

content.p: This Chapter applies to:
regulated Australian vessels; and
foreign vessels; and
such other vessels as are prescribed by the regulations.

section.heading: Certain vessels taken to be registered

content.p: For the purposes of this Chapter, an unregistered vessel flying the flag of a country is taken to be registered in that country.
If a vessel is in the course of construction, or the construction of a vessel has been completed, and the vessel:
has not been registered and is not flying the flag of a country; and
is intended to be registered in a particular country;
the vessel is taken, for the purposes of this Chapter, to be registered in that country.

section.heading: Tonnage regulations

content.p: The regulations may make provision:
giving effect to the Tonnage Convention; and
otherwise in relation to the tonnage of vessels.
Without limiting subsection (1), the regulations may make provision in relation to the following:
issuing International Tonnage Certificates (1969);
issuing other tonnage measurement certificates;
assigning tonnages to vessels;
measuring of tonnage of vessels.

section.heading: Applications for tonnage certificates

content.p: A person may apply to an issuing body for a tonnage certificate of a kind specified in the regulations for a vessel to which this Chapter applies.
The application must be in accordance with the regulations.

section.heading: Issuing body to issue tonnage certificates

content.p: An issuing body may issue a tonnage certificate for a vessel if:
an application for the tonnage certificate has been made to the issuing body under section 154; and
the issuing body is satisfied that the criteria prescribed by the regulations in relation to the issue of the tonnage certificate are met.
A tonnage certificate is subject to:
the conditions (if any) prescribed by the regulations; and
the conditions (if any) imposed by the issuing body.

section.heading: Issuing body may vary tonnage certificates

content.p: An issuing body may vary a tonnage certificate under this section if the issuing body is satisfied that the criteria prescribed by the regulations in relation to the variation of the certificate are met.
Without limiting subsection (1), an issuing body may vary a tonnage certificate to impose, vary or remove a condition on the certificate.

section.heading: Revocation of tonnage certificates

content.p: An issuing body may revoke a tonnage certificate if the issuing body is satisfied that the criteria prescribed by the regulations are met in relation to the revocation of the certificate.

part.heading: Additional provisions relating to non-Tonnage Convention vessels

section.heading: Register tonnage of non-Tonnage Convention vessels that are registered

content.p: Register tonnage of vessel registered in prescribed country

The register tonnage specified in the certificate of registry of a non-Tonnage Convention vessel registered in a country prescribed by the regulations is taken, for the purposes of this Act, to be the register tonnage of the vessel.
Register tonnage of vessel registered in a country other than a prescribed country

The register tonnage of a non-Tonnage Convention vessel that is registered in a country that is not a country prescribed by the regulations is taken, for the purposes of this Act, to be the register tonnage of the vessel determined in accordance with the regulations.

section.heading: Tonnage of non-Tonnage Convention vessels to be measured in certain cases

content.p: If:
an unregistered non-Tonnage Convention vessel enters an Australian port; or
a dispute arises as to the tonnage of a non-Tonnage Convention vessel;
the tonnage of the vessel is to be measured in accordance with the regulations.

section.heading: Assignment of other tonnages to non-Tonnage Convention vessels

content.p: The regulations may assign to a non-Tonnage Convention vessel a gross tonnage and a register tonnage, instead of the gross tonnage and register tonnage ascertained in relation to the vessel in accordance with the other provisions of those regulations.
If the regulations assign to a non-Tonnage Convention vessel a gross tonnage and a register tonnage as mentioned in subsection (1), this Act applies in relation to the vessel as if:
references in this Act to gross tonnage were references to the gross tonnage so assigned; and
references in this Act to register tonnage were references to the register tonnage so assigned.

section.heading: Simplified outline of this Chapter

content.p: This Chapter deals with the safety of navigation.
Part 2 deals with pilotage for certain vessels. It includes provisions relating to the following:
establishing the requirements for compulsory pilotage and a procedure for seeking exemptions from the requirements;
providing for the issue of licences;
providing for pilots to issue certificates as evidence of the provision of pilotage;
the approval and duties of pilotage providers;
establishing offences and civil penalties for navigation without a licensed pilot, failure to comply with exemption conditions and false representation as a licensed pilot;
providing for the reporting of movement or intended movement of vessels.
Part 3 deals with prevention of collisions.
Part 4 imposes obligations to render assistance and report incidents.
Part 5 deals with aids to navigation. It includes provisions:
empowering AMSA to acquire, establish, maintain and inspect aids to navigation; and
empowering AMSA to deal with things that may interfere with safe navigation; and
establishing offences and civil penalty provisions for the fouling or destruction of, or damage to or interference with, aids to navigation.
Part 6 deals with safe navigation. It includes provisions about the following:
vessel traffic services (Division 2);
mandatory routeing (Division 3);
reporting of movement of vessels (Division 4);
the Australian Hydrographic Office (Division 5).

division.heading: Vessels to which this Part applies

section.heading: Vessels to which this Part applies

content.p: This Part applies to a vessel:
that is 70 metres or longer in length overall; or
that is a loaded:
oil tanker; or
chemical carrier; or
liquefied gas carrier.
This Part applies to pilots and pilotage in relation to vessels referred to in subsection (1):
that are in, or in transit to or from, any waters of the coastal sea of Australia prescribed by the regulations; or
that are in any waters of the exclusive economic zone of Australia prescribed by the regulations.

This Part is not intended to affect the operation of any law of a State or Territory governing pilots or pilotage in relation to a port in the State or Territory that is capable of operating concurrently with this Part.

division.heading: Regulations relating to pilotage etc.

section.heading: Regulations relating to compulsory pilotage

content.p: The regulations may make provision in relation to compulsory pilotage, including prescribing waters that are compulsory pilotage areas for the purposes of this Part.
The waters that may be prescribed for the purposes of subsection (1) must be waters included within the waters prescribed by the regulations made for the purposes of subsection 162(2).

section.heading: Regulations relating to licensing of pilots and pilotage providers

content.p: The regulations may make provision in relation to the licensing of pilots and pilotage providers, including standards of competence to be attained and other conditions to be satisfied by a person in order to be licensed as a pilot or a pilotage provider.
Pilots
Without limiting subsection (1), the regulations may make provision in relation to:
conditions as to age, character, medical fitness, nationality, citizenship or residence relating to the licensing of pilots; and
the instruction, training and examination of pilots, including:
the gaining of sea service and other experience; and
the conduct of examinations; and
the conditions for admission to examinations; and
the appointment and remuneration of examiners.
Pilotage providers and pilots
Without limiting subsection (1), the regulations may make provision in relation to the following:
the manner in which the attainment of a standard or the satisfaction of a condition is to be evidenced;
the issue, recall, surrender, replacement, form and recording of licences of pilots and pilotage providers;
the duration, variation, renewal, suspension and cancellation of such licences.

section.heading: Regulations relating to operations of licensed pilots and licensed pilotage providers

content.p: The regulations may make provision in relation to the operations of licensed pilots and licensed pilotage providers.
Without limiting subsection (1), the regulations may make provision in relation to the following:
the duties of a licensed pilot or a licensed pilotage provider and the manner of discharging those duties;
the professional relationship between:
a licensed pilot and officers of a vessel; and
a licensed pilotage provider and a licensed pilot;
the provision of equipment or information by a licensed pilotage provider to a licensed pilot;
matters relating to pilotage safety management systems including the content and implementation of such systems;
the keeping of records;
the training of pilots;
the monitoring of the performance of licensed pilots and licensed pilotage providers;
the professional liability of licensed pilots and licensed pilotage providers and the limitation of that liability;
auditing and monitoring of licensed pilots and licensed pilotage providers.

division.heading: Requirement to navigate with a licensed pilot

section.heading: Navigating without a licensed pilot

content.p: A person contravenes this subsection if:
the person is the master or owner of a vessel; and
the vessel navigates without a licensed pilot in a compulsory pilotage area.
Exceptions
Subsection (1) does not apply to a person if:
the vessel was exempted under section 172 from the requirement to navigate with a licensed pilot in the area; and
the navigation complied with the terms of the exemption.
Subsection (1) does not apply to a person if the vessel navigated in a compulsory pilotage area because of saving life at sea or other unavoidable cause.

Subsection (1) does not apply to the owner of the vessel if he or she took all reasonable precautions to ensure that the vessel would not navigate in a compulsory pilotage area in contravention of that subsection.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 600 penalty units.
Note: The defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subsections (2), (3) and (4) (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 6,000 penalty units.
A person who wishes to rely on subsection (2), (3) or (4) in proceedings for a civil penalty order bears a legal burden in relation to the matters in the subsection concerned.

section.heading: Offences against section 166 by masters of foreign vessels

content.p: Section 9 does not apply to an offence against section 166.
The master of a foreign vessel does not commit an offence against section 166 unless, at the time of the act or omission constituting the alleged offence, the vessel is:
in an Australian port; or
entering or leaving an Australian port; or
in the internal waters of Australia; or
in the territorial sea of Australia.

section.heading: Representations about being a licensed pilot or pilotage provider

content.p: A person must not make a representation that the person is a licensed pilot or a licensed pilotage provider if the person is not a licensed pilot or a licensed pilotage provider.
Strict liability offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 60 penalty units.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.

section.heading: Unlicensed person performing duties of licensed pilot or pilotage provider

content.p: A person contravenes this subsection if:
the person performs duties of a licensed pilot or a licensed pilotage provider that are prescribed by the regulations; and
the person is not a licensed pilot or a licensed pilotage provider, as the case may be.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 60 penalty units.
For the purposes of subsection (2), strict liability applies to paragraph (1)(b).
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.

section.heading: Licensed pilots to issue certificates

content.p: If a licensed pilot has provided pilotage for a vessel in a compulsory pilotage area, the licensed pilot must give the master of the vessel a certificate in the approved form.
The licensed pilot must give the certificate to the master before disembarking from the vessel after the navigation in the area.

section.heading: Engaging an unqualified person to perform duties of licensed pilot

content.p: (1) A person (the first person) contravenes this subsection if:
the first person engages another person to perform the duties of a licensed pilot under the regulations; and
the other person is not a licensed pilot.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 2 years or 120 penalty units, or both.
For the purposes of subsection (2), strict liability applies to paragraph (1)(b).
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 1,200 penalty units.

division.heading: Exemption from requirement to navigate with a licensed pilot

section.heading: Application for exemption

content.p: The master or an owner of a vessel may apply to AMSA for an exemption from the requirement to navigate the vessel with a licensed pilot in a compulsory pilotage area.
The application must:
be in writing; and
contain the information prescribed by the regulations; and
be in the approved form.
AMSA must, after considering the application:
by instrument in writing, grant or refuse to grant the exemption applied for; and
give the applicant a copy of the instrument and, in the case of a refusal, a statement of the reasons for that refusal.

A refusal to grant the exemption applied for may be a refusal to grant the exemption at all or a refusal to grant the exemption as to a part of the vessel’s proposed navigation in the compulsory pilotage area.
An exemption under subsection (1) is subject to the conditions specified in the exemption.
An instrument under this section granting or refusing an exemption is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Failure to comply with conditions of exemption

content.p: A person contravenes this subsection if:
the person is the master or an owner of a vessel; and
the vessel is navigating in a compulsory pilotage area; and
AMSA has granted an exemption from the requirement to navigate with a licensed pilot in respect of the navigation by the vessel in that area; and
the vessel, in navigating in that area, contravenes a condition to which the exemption is subject.

Subsection (1) does not apply to the owner of the vessel if he or she took all reasonable precautions to ensure that the vessel would not navigate in a compulsory pilotage area in contravention of that subsection.
Subsection (1) does not apply if the vessel navigated in a compulsory pilotage area because of stress of weather, saving life at sea or other unavoidable cause.
Strict liability offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 60 penalty units.
Note 1: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
Note 2: The defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subsections (2) and (3) (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.
A person who wishes to rely on subsection (2) or (3) in proceedings for a civil penalty order bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in the subsection concerned.

division.heading: Relationship with the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Act 1975

section.heading: Part is in addition to the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Act 1975

content.p: (1) This Part operates in addition to, and does not limit, any requirement for compulsory pilotage under the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Act 1975 within the compulsory pilotage area under that Act.
(2) A person is not liable to be prosecuted under this Act and the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Act 1975 in respect of the same act or omission.

division.heading: Vessels to which this Part applies

section.heading: Vessels to which this Part applies

content.p: Vessels on the high seas
This Part applies to a vessel on the high seas, if the vessel is any of the following:
a regulated Australian vessel;
a domestic commercial vessel;
a recreational vessel that has Australian nationality.
Vessels not on the high seas
This Part applies to:
a regulated Australian vessel; or
a foreign vessel; or
a domestic commercial vessel; or
a recreational vessel;
if the vessel is situated in any of the following areas:
waters within the territorial sea of Australia;
unless the vessel is a foreign vessel or a recreational vessel that does not have Australian nationality—waters in the exclusive economic zone of Australia;
so far as the provision concerned gives effect to the Prevention of Collisions Convention:
the waters of the sea on the landward side of the territorial sea; or
waters within Australia other than waters of the sea.

division.heading: Collisions, lights and signals

section.heading: Power to make regulations relating to collisions, lights and signals

content.p: The regulations may make provision in relation to requirements for the prevention of collisions and may make provision in relation to the provision and use of lights and signals on vessels.
Without limiting subsection (1), the regulations may make provision in relation to giving effect to the Prevention of Collisions Convention.
The regulations may make provision in relation to:
liability for loss of life or injury to a person on board a vessel because of the fault of the vessel and one or more other vessels; and
the division of liability for loss if 2 or more vessels are involved or at fault in a collision; and
the right of contribution in relation to a collision involving 2 or more vessels that results in loss of life or injury to a person on board a vessel.
Regulations made for the purposes of subsection (3) may, despite section 10, be expressed to apply to a vessel referred to in paragraph 10(a) that is operated by Australia.

division.heading: Operating a vessel in contravention of regulations

section.heading: Operating a vessel in contravention of the regulations—owner

content.p: The owner of a vessel must not operate the vessel, or cause or permit another person to operate the vessel, if the operation of the vessel contravenes regulations made for the purposes of section 176.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 10 years or 600 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 6,000 penalty units.

section.heading: Operating a vessel in contravention of the regulations—master

content.p: The master of a vessel must not operate the vessel, or cause or permit another person to operate the vessel, if the operation of the vessel contravenes regulations made for the purposes of section 176.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 10 years or 600 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 6,000 penalty units.

division.heading: No presumption of fault

section.heading: No presumption of fault

content.p: If a collision occurs involving one or more vessels:
a vessel is not taken to be at fault merely because of a contravention of this Part in relation to the vessel; and
the collision is not taken to have been caused by the wrongful act, neglect, or default of a seafarer of a vessel merely because of a contravention of this Part in relation to the vessel.

part.heading: Obligation to render assistance and report incidents

division.heading: Vessels to which this Part applies

section.heading: Vessels to which this Part applies

content.p: This Part applies to the following:
a regulated Australian vessel;
a foreign vessel;
a domestic commercial vessel;
a recreational vessel.

division.heading: Obligation to render assistance

section.heading: Obligation to render assistance

content.p: The master of a vessel contravenes this subsection if:
the vessel is at sea; and
the master has reason to believe that one or more persons are in distress at sea; and
the master does not both:
cause the vessel to proceed as fast as practicable to the assistance of the person or persons; and
inform the person or persons that the master is doing so.
Subsection (1) does not apply if:
the master is unable to comply with paragraph (1)(c); or
in the special circumstances of the case, it is unreasonable or unnecessary for the master to comply with paragraph (1)(c); or
the master of the vessel is informed by the person or persons in distress, or by the master of another vessel, that assistance is no longer necessary; or
the master is informed that another vessel has been requisitioned and is complying with the requisition.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 4 years.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in subsection (2) (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).

section.heading: Obligation to render assistance if requisitioned

content.p: The master of a vessel that is in distress at sea may, after consulting so far as possible with the masters of vessels that answer his or her call for assistance, requisition a vessel that the master considers best able to render assistance.
The master of a vessel contravenes this subsection if:
the vessel is requisitioned under subsection (1) by the master of another vessel that is in distress at sea; and
the master does not cause his or her vessel to proceed as fast as practicable to the assistance of the other vessel.
Subsection (2) does not apply if:
the master is unable to comply with paragraph (2)(b); or
in the special circumstances of the case, it is unreasonable or unnecessary for the master to comply with paragraph (2)(b); or
the master of the vessel is informed by the person or persons in distress, or by the master of another vessel, that assistance is no longer necessary; or
the master is informed that another vessel has been requisitioned and is complying with the requisition.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (2).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 10 years.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in subsection (3) (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).
Requisition to assist vessel to which this Part does not apply
The master of a vessel in distress may requisition a vessel under this section even if the vessel in distress is not a vessel to which this Part applies.

section.heading: Offences against sections 181 and 182 by masters of foreign vessels

content.p: Section 9 does not apply to an offence against section 181 or 182.
The master of a foreign vessel does not commit an offence against section 181 or 182 unless, at the time of the act or omission constituting the alleged offence, the vessel is:
in an Australian port; or
entering or leaving an Australian port; or
in the internal waters of Australia; or
in the territorial sea of Australia.

section.heading: Obligation to record requests for assistance

content.p: The master of a vessel contravenes this subsection if the master:
receives information that a person or persons are in distress at sea, and does not proceed to the assistance of the person or persons in distress; and
is required by any law to keep a logbook for the vessel; and
does not record in the vessel’s logbook his or her reasons for not so proceeding.
Strict liability offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Reporting of marine incidents to AMSA—owner

content.p: An owner of a vessel contravenes this subsection if:
the vessel is involved in a marine incident that has affected, or is likely to affect, the safety, operation or seaworthiness of the vessel; and

neither the owner nor the master of the vessel gives a written report of the incident in the approved form to AMSA, within the period prescribed by the regulations, after the owner becomes aware of the incident.
An owner of a vessel contravenes this subsection if:
the vessel is involved in, or causes, a marine incident that involves:
the death of a person; or
serious injury to a person; or
the loss of a vessel; or
the loss of a person from the vessel; or
significant damage to a vessel; or
loss of cargo of a vessel; and
neither the owner nor the master of the vessel reports the incident to AMSA, within the period prescribed by the regulations, after the owner becomes aware of the incident.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1) or (2).
Penalty: 60 penalty units.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1) or (2).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.

section.heading: Reporting of marine incidents to AMSA—master

content.p: The master of a vessel contravenes this subsection if:
the vessel is involved in a marine incident that has affected, or is likely to affect, the safety, operation or seaworthiness of the vessel; and

Penalty: 60 penalty units.
The master of a vessel contravenes this subsection if:

serious injury to a person; or

Civil penalty

section.heading: Report of dangers to navigation

content.p: The master of a vessel contravenes this subsection if:
the master meets with, or is informed of, any serious danger to navigation on or near his or her course; and
the master does not, at the earliest practicable time:

(i) send out to vessels in the vicinity, by all means of communication available to him or her, the safety signal prescribed by the regulations, followed by a message (the danger message) conveying such information as is prescribed by the regulations; and
make a report to shore to the person prescribed by the regulations, and in the manner prescribed by the regulations.
Subsection (1) does not apply if compliance with that subsection would interfere with the transmission of a signal of distress.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 12 months or 60 penalty units, or both.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in subsection (2) (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.
Evidential burden
A person who wishes to rely on subsection (2) in proceedings for a civil penalty order bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in that subsection.
Serious danger to navigation
The reference in subsection (1) to a serious danger to navigation includes, but is not limited to, any of the following:
dangerous ice;
a dangerous derelict;
a tropical storm;
sub-freezing air temperature associated with gale force winds causing severe ice accretion on superstructures;

Transmission to be free of cost
The transmission under this section of danger messages or safety signals is to be free of cost to the vessels concerned.

division.heading: Regulations

section.heading: Regulations relating to aids to navigation

content.p: The regulations may make provision in relation to aids to navigation.

division.heading: AMSA’s powers in relation to aids to navigation

section.heading: Acquisition of aids to navigation by compulsory process

content.p: This section applies if AMSA is unable to enter into an agreement with a State or Territory for the acquisition of any particular aid to navigation belonging to that State or Territory.
The Minister may acquire by compulsory process:
the aid to navigation; and
any other property used in connection with the aid to navigation; and
so much of the land (if any) required or used for the purpose of the aid to navigation as AMSA thinks sufficient.

(3) The provisions of the Lands Acquisition Act 1989 relating to the acquisition of interests in land by compulsory process and to the determination of the amount of compensation payable in respect of interests so acquired apply, so far as applicable, in relation to the acquisition of property under this section.

section.heading: Power to establish, maintain and inspect aids to navigation

content.p: AMSA may:
establish and maintain aids to navigation; and
add to, alter or remove any aid to navigation that is owned or controlled by AMSA; and
vary the character of any aid to navigation that is owned or controlled by AMSA.
AMSA, or a person authorised in writing by AMSA may, at any reasonable time of the day or night:

inspect any aid to navigation or any lamp or light which, in the opinion of AMSA or the authorised person, may affect the safety or convenience of navigation, whether the aid to navigation or the lamp or light is the property of:
a State or Territory; or
an agency of a State or Territory; or
any other person; and
enter any property, whether public or private, for the purposes of an inspection under paragraph (a); and
transport, or cause to be transported, any goods through any property, whether public or private, for any purpose in connection with:
the maintenance of an aid to navigation that is owned or controlled by AMSA; or
the establishment of any aid to navigation by AMSA.

section.heading: Other powers in relation to aids to navigation

content.p: If in AMSA’s opinion it is desirable for the safety of navigation to do so, AMSA may, by notice in writing given to the owner of an aid to navigation, or a lamp or light, require the owner of the aid, lamp or light:
before the end of the period specified in the notice—to remove it entirely or to move it to another position; or
before the end of the period specified in the notice—to modify it or to alter its character to such an extent and in such a manner as AMSA specifies in the notice; or
in the case of a lamp or light, with effect from a day specified in the notice:
to refrain from lighting the lamp or light either entirely or for the period AMSA specifies in the notice; or
to cease showing the lamp or light either entirely or for the period AMSA specifies in the notice.
The period specified in a notice referred to in paragraph (1)(a) or (b) must be at least 14 days, other than in exceptional circumstances relating to the safety of persons or vessels.
If the notice is not complied with, AMSA may do in regard to the aid to navigation, lamp or light anything that the owner was required by the notice to do.
Any expense incurred by AMSA under this section may be recovered by AMSA from the owner, as a debt due by the owner to AMSA.
In this section:
owner, of an aid to navigation, lamp or light, includes a State or Territory government, or any agency of a State or Territory, that has the control or management of the aid, lamp or light.
A notice under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Returns of aids to navigation

content.p: A harbour authority or other local authority that has control of any aid to navigation must notify AMSA of the following matters:
the description and situation of each aid to navigation under its control;
any change to the characteristics of an aid to navigation that could affect the safety of navigation.
A notification under subsection (1) in relation to an aid to navigation must be made:
when the aid to navigation first commences operation; and
when the aid to navigation is decommissioned; and
when a change referred to in paragraph (1)(b) occurs.
A notification under subsection (1) must be in accordance with the regulations.
Strict liability offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 30 penalty units.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

division.heading: Offences and civil penalties relating to aids to navigation

content.p: Subdivision A—Failure to comply with notice

section.heading: Failure to comply with a notice about aids to navigation

content.p: A person contravenes this subsection if:

Subsection (1) does not apply if the person has a reasonable excuse.
Strict liability offence

Subdivision B—Destruction etc. of aids to navigation

section.heading: Intentionally destroying, fouling or damaging aids to navigation

content.p: A person contravenes this subsection if:
the person does an act or omits to do an act; and
the act or omission results in:
the destruction or fouling of an AMSA aid to navigation; or
damage to, or reduction in or limitation of the effectiveness of, an AMSA aid to navigation; and
the person intends that the act or omission will have that result.
Subsection (1) does not apply if:
the act or omission was necessary to save a life or a vessel, or to prevent pollution; and
the person took all reasonable steps to avoid the destruction, fouling, damage, reduction or limitation.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 10 years or 600 penalty units, or both.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in subsection (2) (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 6,000 penalty units.

section.heading: Notice of damage to aid to navigation

content.p: Section 9 does not apply to:

division.heading: Additional matters relating to aids to navigation

section.heading: Liability for damage, etc.

content.p: If a person is convicted of an offence, or found to have contravened a civil penalty provision, under Division 3, an eligible court may (in addition to imposing a penalty on the person) order the person to pay an amount up to:
the amount of the damage caused by the offence or contravention; or
the cost of repairing, replacing or reinstating the aid to navigation.
If an AMSA aid to navigation is removed, damaged or destroyed by a person, the person is liable to pay to AMSA the cost of repairing, replacing or reinstating the AMSA aid to navigation.

If an AMSA aid to navigation is removed, damaged or destroyed by a vessel, the master and owner of the vessel are jointly and severally liable to pay to AMSA the cost of repairing, replacing or reinstating the AMSA aid to navigation.

section.heading: Transfer of aids to navigation to be valid

content.p: This section applies if AMSA has entered into an agreement with a State, a Territory or any other person, for the acquisition by AMSA of an aid to navigation.

division.heading: Preliminary

section.heading: Vessels to which this Part applies

content.p: This Part applies to:

division.heading: Vessel traffic services

section.heading: Regulations relating to vessel traffic services

content.p: The regulations may make provision in relation to vessel traffic services.
Without limiting subsection (1), the regulations may make provision in relation to the following:
establishment and recognition of vessel traffic services;
authorisation by AMSA of vessel traffic services;
testing of vessel traffic services;
training, certification and auditing in relation to vessel traffic services;
provision of reports and information to a vessel traffic service authority by specified persons in relation to the identity, intended passage and geographical location of vessels;
the form of such reports and information and the period within which such reports are to be provided.

section.heading: Liability of master or owner under vessel traffic service arrangements

content.p: The master of a vessel is not relieved from responsibility for the conduct and navigation of the vessel merely because the vessel is subject to vessel traffic service arrangements.

A requirement under a law of the Commonwealth or of a State or Territory that vessel traffic service arrangements be complied with does not affect the liability of the owner or master of a vessel that complies with such arrangements for:
loss or damage caused by the vessel; or
loss or damage caused by a fault of the navigation of the vessel.

section.heading: Reports must be provided to a vessel traffic service authority

content.p: A person contravenes this subsection if:
the person is required by the regulations to provide a report or information to a vessel traffic service authority; and
the person does not provide the report or information.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 240 penalty units.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 2,400 penalty units.

section.heading: False or misleading information provided to a vessel traffic service authority

content.p: A person contravenes this subsection if:

A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).

Civil penalty

subsection 215(1) or 216(1).
The master or owner of a foreign vessel, or a recreational vessel that does not have Australian nationality:
does not commit an offence against a provision referred to in paragraph (1)(a) that relates to the vessel; and
is not liable for a civil penalty because of a contravention of a provision referred to in paragraph (1)(b) that relates to the vessel;
unless, at the time of the act or omission constituting the alleged offence or contravention, the vessel concerned is:
in an Australian port; or
entering or leaving an Australian port; or
in the internal waters of Australia; or
in the territorial sea of Australia; or
in the exclusive economic zone of Australia.

division.heading: Mandatory routeing

section.heading: Mandatory ship routeing systems

content.p: The master of a vessel contravenes this subsection if:
a mandatory ship routeing system applies to the vessel; and
the master does not navigate in accordance with the system.
Subsection (1) does not apply if the master did not navigate in accordance with the mandatory ship routeing system because of stress of weather, saving life at sea or other unavoidable cause.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 12 months or 60 penalty units, or both.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in subsection (2) (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.
A person who wishes to rely on subsection (2) in proceedings for a civil penalty order bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in that subsection.

section.heading: Geographical application

content.p: Section 9 does not apply to:
an offence against subsection 218(3); or
a contravention of subsection 218(1), so far as it is a civil penalty provision.
The master of a foreign vessel or a recreational vessel that does not have Australian nationality:
does not commit an offence against subsection 218(3) that relates to the vessel; and
is not liable for a civil penalty for a contravention of subsection 218(1) that relates to the vessel;
unless, at the time of the act or omission constituting the alleged offence or contravention, the vessel concerned is:
in an Australian port; or
entering or leaving an Australian port; or
in the internal waters of Australia; or
in the territorial sea of Australia; or
in the exclusive economic zone of Australia.

section.heading: Navigation not in accordance with mandatory ship routeing system to be entered in log

content.p: The master of a vessel contravenes this subsection if:
a mandatory ship routeing system applies to the vessel; and
the master does not navigate in accordance with the system; and
if the master of the vessel is required to keep a logbook for the vessel—the master does not enter details of that navigation in the vessel’s logbook.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 100 penalty units.

division.heading: Reporting of movement of vessels

section.heading: Regulations relating to reporting requirements

content.p: The regulations may make provision for the reporting requirements:
of foreign vessels that are in, or in the process of entering or leaving, the prescribed area in relation to a reporting matter; and
of all regulated Australian vessels in any area.
Without limiting subsection (1), the regulations may provide for:
the form and content of sailing plans for foreign vessels proposing to leave an Australian port bound for another port, whether or not the other port is an Australian port; and
the form and content of sailing plans for regulated Australian vessels proposing to leave a port bound for another port, whether or not the ports are Australian ports; and

the form and content of reports on the movement of foreign vessels entering, traversing or leaving the prescribed area in relation to a reporting matter, including reports on position, course and speed and such other matters as the regulations prescribe; and
the form and content of reports on the movement of regulated Australian vessels, including reports on position, course and speed and such other matters as the regulations prescribe; and

the requirement to notify the cancellation of sailing plans and to give additional reports on movement if a vessel deviates, by more than an amount prescribed by the regulations, from a previously indicated course; and
the time at which and manner in which sailing plans, reports on movements and cancellations of sailing plans are to be notified.
In this section:
prescribed area, in relation to any reporting matter or matters, means an area of sea around Australia that comprises so much of:
the area for which Australia has responsibility for search and rescue; and

any area of the sea beyond the outer limits of the area referred to in paragraph (a) that is an area in respect of which Australia is required or permitted, under an international instrument, to obtain reports relating to the movement, or intended movement, of vessels;
as is prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this Division in relation to that matter or those matters.

reporting matter means any matter relating to the movement, or intended movement, of vessels, including any such matter that is referred to under an international instrument that confers rights or imposes duties on Australia as a contracting party.

section.heading: Geographical application

content.p: Section 9 does not apply to:
an offence against a regulation made under section 221; or
a civil penalty provision in regulations made for the purposes of section 221.
The master or owner of a foreign vessel or a recreational vessel that does not have Australian nationality:
does not commit an offence against a regulation made for the purposes of section 221 that relates to the vessel; and
is not liable for a civil penalty for a contravention of such a regulation that relates to the vessel;
unless at the time of the act or omission constituting the alleged offence or contravention, the vessel concerned is:
in an Australian port; or
entering or leaving an Australian port; or
in the internal waters of Australia; or
in the territorial sea of Australia; or
in the exclusive economic zone of Australia.

division.heading: The Australian Hydrographic Office and offences and civil penalties relating to taking a vessel to sea without charts, etc.

section.heading: Functions of the Australian Hydrographic Office

content.p: The Australian Hydrographic Office is that part of the Department of Defence known as the Australian Hydrographic Office.
The functions of the Australian Hydrographic Office are:
to be responsible for the provision of hydrographic services required by the Safety Convention; and
to collect, compile and collate hydrographic data; and
to maintain and disseminate hydrographic and other nautical information and nautical publications; and
to maintain and disseminate nautical charts, including authorising charts for use in Australian waters.

section.heading: Taking a vessel to sea without nautical charts and publications—owner

content.p: The owner of a regulated Australian vessel or a foreign vessel must not take the vessel to sea, or cause or permit another person to take the vessel to sea, if:
the vessel is not supplied with:
nautical charts (including charts in electronic form), of a suitable scale and properly corrected at the time of sailing; and
nautical publications;
necessary for use on the particular voyage; or
the vessel is supplied with the charts and publications referred to in paragraph (a), but free access to them is not made available to seafarers involved in the navigation of the vessel.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 12 months or 60 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.

section.heading: Taking a vessel to sea without nautical charts and publications—master

content.p: The master of a regulated Australian vessel or a foreign vessel must not take the vessel to sea, or cause or permit another person to take the vessel to sea, if:
the vessel is not supplied with:
nautical charts (including charts in electronic form), of a suitable scale and properly corrected at the time of sailing; and
nautical publications;
necessary for use on the particular voyage; or
the vessel is supplied with the charts and publications referred to in paragraph (a), but free access to them is not made available to seafarers involved in the navigation of the vessel.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 12 months or 60 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.

section.heading: Simplified outline of this Chapter

content.p: This Chapter deals with wrecks and salvage.
Part 2 provides for the establishment of a regime for notifying wrecks and dealing with wrecks.
Part 3 provides for the following:
giving effect to the Salvage Convention;
determining the scope of salvage operations that are subject to this Act;
salvage claims by, or against, the Crown.

division.heading: Wrecks to which this Part applies

section.heading: Wrecks to which this Part applies

content.p: This Part applies to any wreck of or from:
regulated Australian vessels; and
foreign vessels.

division.heading: Rights and powers in relation to wrecks

section.heading: Right of Commonwealth to unclaimed wreck

content.p: The Commonwealth is entitled to all unclaimed wreck found in Australia.

section.heading: Dealing with wrecks

content.p: AMSA has the following powers in relation to any wreck:
to require, by written notice, the legal owner of the wreck, within the period specified in the notice:
to remove the wreck, or a specified part of the wreck; or
to give security to the satisfaction of AMSA for such removal;
to require, by written notice, the legal owner of the wreck, within the period specified in the notice:
to mark the wreck, or a specified part of the wreck; or
to give security to the satisfaction of AMSA for such marking;
to mark or remove the wreck, or a part of the wreck, in any manner it sees fit, if:
AMSA considers it necessary for the purposes of saving human life, securing the safe navigation of vessels or protecting the marine environment; or
there is no legal owner of the wreck, or AMSA cannot, despite making reasonable efforts, locate or contact the legal owner; or
the legal owner does not comply with a notice given to him or her under paragraph (a) or (b) within the period specified in the notice;

to destroy or sink the wreck, or a part of the wreck, in any manner it sees fit, if AMSA considers it necessary for the purposes of saving human life, securing the safe navigation of vessels or protecting the marine environment;
to recover from the legal owner of the wreck any expenses incurred by AMSA in connection with locating, marking, removing, destroying or sinking the wreck.
AMSA may exercise the powers in paragraphs (1)(a) and (b) in respect of the following:
a wreck of, or wreck from, a regulated Australian vessel wherever it is situated;
a wreck of, or wreck from, a foreign vessel situated in the territorial sea of Australia.
AMSA may exercise the powers referred to in paragraphs (1)(c) and (d) in respect of the following:
a wreck of, or wreck from, a regulated Australian vessel situated:
in the exclusive economic zone of Australia; or
in the territorial sea of Australia;
a wreck of, or wreck from, a foreign vessel situated in the territorial sea of Australia.
A notice under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Person must comply with notice

content.p: A legal owner of any wreck contravenes this subsection if:
the owner is required under subsection 229(1) to remove or mark the wreck, or a specified part of the wreck; and
the owner fails to comply with the requirement.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 600 penalty units.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 6,000 penalty units.

section.heading: Powers to pass over land and require assistance etc.

content.p: AMSA may gain access to any wreck, including by crossing land without the consent of the occupier of the land, for the purpose of rendering assistance or saving life.
AMSA may deposit any wreck on land without the consent of the occupier of the land.
A person must not impede AMSA in exercising its powers under subsection (1) or (2).
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (3).
Penalty: 5 years imprisonment or 300 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (3).
Civil penalty: 3,000 penalty units.

section.heading: Notification about wrecks

content.p: The master or owner of any vessel that is wrecked, stranded, sunk or abandoned or has foundered must notify AMSA within the period prescribed by the regulations of the following matters:
the name and principal place of business of the owner of the vessel;
the location of the vessel;
the type, size and construction of the vessel;
the nature and quantity of cargo and any hazardous or noxious substances on board the vessel;
the amount and type of oil, including bunker and lubricating oil, on board the vessel.
Subsection (1) does not apply to a foreign vessel if it is not situated in the territorial sea of Australia.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 60 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in subsection (2) (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.
A person who wishes to rely on subsection (2) in proceedings for a civil penalty order bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in that subsection.

section.heading: Finding or taking possession of wreck

content.p: A person who finds or takes possession of any wreck in, or brings any wreck into, the territorial sea of Australia must give notice to AMSA within the period prescribed by the regulations:
that the person has found or taken possession of the wreck or brought the wreck into the territorial sea of Australia; and
of the location of the wreck and the marks by which it may be recognised.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 60 penalty units.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 180 penalty units.

section.heading: AMSA must give notice of wreck

content.p: This section applies if AMSA is given a notice under section 232 or 233 in relation to a vessel or any wreck, or otherwise becomes aware of any wreck.

AMSA must, as soon as reasonably practicable after being given the notice, or becoming aware of the wreck, publish a notice on its website or in a nautical publication prescribed by the regulations that sets out the details prescribed by the regulations relating to the vessel or wreck.

section.heading: Defacing or obliterating marks on a wreck

content.p: A person must not do an act, or omit to do an act, if the act or omission results, or is likely to result, in the defacement or obliteration of a mark on:
a wreck of, or wreck from, a regulated Australian vessel situated:
in the exclusive economic zone of Australia; or
in the territorial sea of Australia; or
a wreck of, or wreck from, a foreign vessel situated in the territorial sea of Australia.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 300 penalty units.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 900 penalty units.

section.heading: Removing a wreck without consent

content.p: A person must not remove any wreck if the person does not have the consent of the legal owner of the wreck or of AMSA.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 1,200 penalty units.
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 6,600 penalty units.

section.heading: Powers of officers of Customs

content.p: This Part does not derogate from or interfere with the powers of an officer of Customs conferred by any Act.

section.heading: Limits on powers to deal with wrecks

content.p: This section applies to the following:
a historic wreck;
a wreck:
that is a historic shipwreck or historic relic within the meaning of a law of a State or of the Northern Territory that relates to shipwrecks or relics of historic significance; and
in relation to which the provisions of that law apply.
AMSA must not exercise any of the powers referred to in section 229 in relation to the wreck unless, in AMSA’s opinion, it is necessary to do so for the purpose of:
saving human life; or
securing the safe navigation of vessels; or
dealing with an emergency involving a serious threat to the environment.

section.heading: Certain provisions not applicable to historic wrecks

content.p: Sections 233 and 236 do not apply to:
a historic wreck; or
a wreck:
that is a historic shipwreck or historic relic within the meaning of a law of a State or of the Northern Territory that relates to shipwrecks or relics of historic significance; and
in relation to which the provisions of that law apply.

division.heading: Vessels to which this Part applies

section.heading: Vessels to which this Part applies

content.p: Subject to subsections (2) and (3), this Part applies:
to all vessels; and
whenever judicial or arbitral proceedings relating to the provision of salvage operations are brought in Australia.

This Part does not apply to fixed or floating platforms or to mobile offshore drilling units when such platforms or units are on location engaged in the exploration, exploitation or production of mineral resources of the seabed or its subsoil.
This Part does not apply to any salvage operation:
that takes place in inland waters and that involves vessels all of which are of inland navigation; or
that takes place in inland waters and does not involve a vessel; or
to the extent that it involves property:
that is maritime cultural property of prehistoric, archaeological or historic interest; and
that is situated on the seabed.
This Part does not derogate from or interfere with the powers of an officer of Customs conferred by any Act.

division.heading: Regulations relating to salvage

section.heading: Regulations relating to salvage

content.p: The regulations may make provision in relation to:
giving effect to the Salvage Convention; and
salvage operations, and claims relating to salvage operations, conducted by or on behalf of the Commonwealth, a State, a Territory or the government of a country prescribed by the regulations.
Without limiting subsection (1), the regulations may make provision in relation to:
the action to be taken with respect to vessels and other property saved as a result of salvage operations conducted by or on behalf of the Commonwealth or a State or Territory; and
the execution of bonds for the payment of salvage operations so conducted; and
the taking of security for the performance of bonds executed under regulations made for the purposes of paragraph (b); and

the adjudication on, and the enforcement of, bonds executed under regulations made for the purposes of paragraph (b) or under a law that is a law of a country prescribed by the regulations and corresponds with regulations made for the purposes of paragraph (b); and
the conditions subject to which claims relating to salvage operations may be made by the seafarers of a Government vessel or a vessel belonging to a foreign country prescribed by the regulations.
(3) A charge that arises under subsection (2) in relation to a vessel has priority over any PPSA security interest within the meaning of the Personal Property Securities Act 2009 in the vessel.
(4) Subsection 73(2) of the Personal Property Securities Act 2009 applies to a charge that arises under subsection (2).

Note: The effect of this subsection is that the priority between a charge that arises under subsection (2) and a PPSA security interest is to be determined in accordance with this Act rather than the Personal Property Securities Act 2009.
Section 10 does not limit this section.

section.heading: Salvage claims against the Crown, etc.

content.p: Subject to subsection (2), regulations made for the purposes of this Part apply in relation to salvage operations conducted:
to save life from, or to assist, a Government vessel—as if the vessel were not a Government vessel; or

to save any wreck, cargo or equipment that belongs to the Commonwealth or a State or Territory—as if the wreck, cargo or equipment belonged to a person other than the Commonwealth, a State or a Territory.

A claim does not lie against the Commonwealth or the Australian Postal Corporation because of this section in respect of anything done or suffered in relation to an article in the course of post, or the contents of an article in the course of post, while the article is or was being carried by sea.
Section 10 does not limit this section.

section.heading: Salvage claims by the Crown, etc.

content.p: If salvage operations are conducted by or on behalf of the Commonwealth, a State, a Territory or the government of a country prescribed by the regulations, the Commonwealth, the State, the Territory or that government is entitled to claim payment in respect of those operations to the same extent, and has the same rights and remedies, as any other salvor.

section.heading: Simplified outline of this Chapter

content.p: This Chapter provides for compliance with, and enforcement of, this Act.
Part 2 confers wide-ranging powers on AMSA to give directions in relation to vessels.
Part 3 deals with the detention of vessels and provides an offence for operating a detained vessel. The Part also empowers an officer of Customs to refuse clearance to vessels.
Part 4 provides for the appointment of inspectors and sets out their powers and functions including the following:
powers to board vessels;
powers of inspection, search and seizure;
powers to issue prohibition and improvement notices.
Part 5 contains provisions that support the civil penalty provisions.
Part 6 relates to infringement notices and voluntary enforceable undertakings.

section.heading: Vessels to which Chapter applies

content.p: This Chapter applies to all vessels.

section.heading: Directions in relation to vessels

content.p: AMSA may, by notice in writing given to the master or the owner of a vessel, give any of the following directions:
that the vessel not enter or use any port, or a specified port or specified ports, in Australia or the exclusive economic zone of Australia;
that the vessel comply with specified requirements while it:
is approaching, entering, or using any port, or a specified port or specified ports, in Australia or the exclusive economic zone of Australia; or
is in or is leaving any port, or a specified port or specified ports, in Australia or the exclusive economic zone of Australia.
AMSA may give a direction under subsection (1) in relation to a foreign vessel only if the vessel is:
in an Australian port; or
entering or leaving an Australian port; or
in the internal waters of Australia; or
in the territorial sea of Australia, other than in the course of innocent passage.
A direction under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Persons must comply with directions

content.p: A person who is given a direction under section 246 must comply with the direction or ensure that the direction is complied with.
Subsection (1) does not apply if non-compliance with the direction is necessary to save a person’s life at sea or is due to an emergency involving a threat to a person’s life.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 10 years or 600 penalty units, or both.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in subsection (2) (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).
Civil penalty
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 6,000 penalty units.
A person who wishes to rely on subsection (2) in proceedings for a civil penalty order bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in that subsection.

section.heading: Power for AMSA to detain

content.p: AMSA may detain a vessel and may also bring it, or cause it to be brought, to a port, or to another place that AMSA considers appropriate, if:
AMSA reasonably suspects that the vessel is unseaworthy or substandard; or
AMSA reasonably suspects that the vessel has been, is or will be involved in a contravention, either in or outside Australia, of this Act; or
AMSA reasonably suspects that a seafarer of the vessel or a person on board the vessel has been, is or will be involved in a contravention, either in or outside Australia, of this Act; or
both of the following apply:

AMSA reasonably suspects that the master of the vessel, or a seafarer of the vessel, would contravene this Act if he or she operated the vessel without a particular certificate or certificates, or other documentary evidence;
the master of the vessel, or the seafarer, does not produce the certificate or certificates or the other documentary evidence to AMSA when requested to do so; or
a provision of this Act provides for AMSA to detain the vessel.
If AMSA detains a vessel under subsection (1), AMSA must give written notice, within 14 days, to:
the master of the vessel; or
the person who had possession or control of the vessel immediately before it was detained.
The notice must:
identify the vessel; and
state that the vessel has been detained; and
specify the reason for the detention; and
specify contact details of an inspector who can provide further information; and
specify any conditions to which the detention of the vessel is subject.
The regulations may make provision in relation to the release of detained vessels.
AMSA may detain a foreign vessel only if the vessel is:
in an Australian port; or
entering or leaving an Australian port; or
in the internal waters of Australia; or
in the territorial sea of Australia, other than in the course of innocent passage.

section.heading: Operating a detained vessel

content.p: A person must not operate a vessel if:
