the nature of the information that will be published; and
the time at which the publication of information will occur.
(3) This section does not permit AMSA to publish information if the publication of the information would contravene the Privacy Act 1988 or another law of the Commonwealth.

section.heading: Penalty for receiving fees for supply of seafarers

content.p: A person must not demand or receive, directly or indirectly, remuneration from an individual for providing or promising to provide the individual with employment as a seafarer on a vessel.
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 30 penalty units.
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 300 penalty units.

section.heading: Compliance of foreign-based foreign Greater Sunrise vessels with international safety and operating standards

content.p: The master and owner of a foreign-based foreign Greater Sunrise vessel must each ensure compliance with requirements described in subsection (2) that apply in relation to the vessel or would apply in relation to it if it had the nationality of a party to a convention mentioned in paragraph (2)(a).
For the purposes of subsection (1), the requirements are those that:
are described in any of the following:
the Prevention of Collisions Convention;
the Load Lines Convention;
the Prevention of Pollution Convention;
the Safety Convention;
the STCW Convention;
the Tonnage Convention;
the Maritime Labour Convention;
the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea;
the Container Convention;
the International Convention on Civil Liability for Bunker Oil Pollution Damage, 2001, done at London on 23 March 2001, as amended and in force for Australia from time to time;
the International Convention for the Control and Management of Ships’ Ballast Water and Sediments, 2004, done at London on 13 February 2004, as amended and in force for Australia from time to time;
the International Convention on the Control of Harmful Anti-Fouling Systems on Ships, 2001, done at London on 5 October 2001, as amended and in force for Australia from time to time; or
both:
reflect international safety or operating standards; and
are prescribed by the regulations.

Note 1: The International Convention on Civil Liability for Bunker Oil Pollution Damage, 2001 is in Australian Treaty Series 2009 No. 14 ([2009] ATS 14) and could in 2019 be viewed in the Australian Treaties Library on the AustLII website (http://www.austlii.edu.au).

Note 2: The International Convention for the Control and Management of Ships’ Ballast Water and Sediments, 2004 is in Australian Treaty Series 2017 No. 15 ([2017] ATS 15) and could in 2019 be viewed in the Australian Treaties Library on the AustLII website (http://www.austlii.edu.au).

Note 3: The International Convention on the Control of Harmful Anti-Fouling Systems on Ships, 2001 is in Australian Treaty Series 2008 No. 15 ([2008] ATS 15) and could in 2019 be viewed in the Australian Treaties Library on the AustLII website (http://www.austlii.edu.au).

section.heading: AMSA may approve form

content.p: AMSA may, in writing, approve a form for the purposes of a provision of this Act.

section.heading: General regulation-making power

content.p: The Governor-General may make regulations prescribing matters:
required or permitted by this Act to be prescribed; or
necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Act.
Without limiting subsection (1), regulations may make provision for or in relation to the following:
design and construction of vessels;
machinery and equipment to be carried on board vessels, including but not limited to the following:
machinery and equipment for sending or receiving distress, urgency and other signals;
radio installations, radio navigational aids and communications equipment;
compasses;
lights;
operating, maintaining, checking and testing any such machinery and equipment;
marking of load lines on vessels;
the stability of vessels including information about, and testing of, the stability of vessels;
operating watertight doors;
saving of life at sea, including:
the equipment to be carried on board vessels; and
measures to be carried out for the purpose of saving life at sea;
prevention, detection and extinguishment of fires at sea, including:
equipment to be carried on board vessels; and
measures to be carried out for the purpose of preventing, detecting and extinguishing fires at sea;
maintenance, testing, survey and certification of vessels;
special purpose vessels;
industrial personnel vessels;
nuclear vessels;
logbooks;
records relating to compliance with this Act;
the exercise of powers, and performance of functions, of issuing bodies under this Act;

(o) matters of a transitional nature (including matters of an application or saving nature) arising out of the enactment of this Act or the repeal of the Navigation Act 1912 or the Lighthouses Act 1911.
Regulations made for the purposes of paragraph (2)(o) may:

(a) provide for specified certificates in force under the Navigation Act 1912 immediately before its repeal to have effect, subject to any specified conditions or limitations, for the purposes of this Act or specified provisions of this Act as if those certificates had been issued under specified provisions of this Act; and

(b) provide for specified things done under the Navigation Act 1912, or under regulations or instruments made under that Act, to have effect, subject to any specified conditions or limitations, for the purposes of this Act or specified provisions of this Act as if those things had been done under specified provisions of this Act; and

(c) provide that all or specified agreements that were in force immediately before the repeal of the Navigation Act 1912 and that, immediately before that repeal complied with one or more specified provisions of Division 8 of Part II of that Act, comply with regulations made for the purposes of subsection 54(5) of this Act, subject to specified limitations.
This subsection does not limit paragraph (2)(o).
To avoid doubt, regulations under this section may be expressed to apply to vessels that are not regulated Australian vessels.

section.heading: Regulation-making power to implement Conventions

content.p: The regulations may make provision in relation to giving effect to the following:
the Safety Convention;
the Prevention of Collisions Convention;
the Prevention of Pollution Convention;
the Load Lines Convention;
the Tonnage Convention;
the Container Convention;
the Limitation of Liability for Maritime Claims Convention;
the STCW Convention;
the Maritime Labour Convention.
Note: Sections 12 and 13 may affect the application of the regulations in certain circumstances relating to the Marine Safety (Domestic Commercial Vessel) National Law or State and Territory law.

Regulations that make provision in relation to giving effect to the Container Convention must not impose, or authorise the imposition of, structural safety requirements or tests on containers to which the Container Convention applies that are not required or permitted by that Convention to be imposed on such containers.
Note: Section 13 may affect the application of the regulations in certain circumstances relating to State and Territory law.
To avoid doubt, regulations made for the purposes of this section may be expressed to apply to vessels that are not regulated Australian vessels.

section.heading: General provisions relating to regulations

content.p: The regulations may provide for:
the imposition of penalties of not more than 50 penalty units for a contravention of:
a provision of the regulations; or
a notice, order, direction or instruction given, issued or made under, or in force because of, the regulations; and
the imposition of civil penalties for a contraventions of a kind referred to in subparagraph (a)(i) or (ii) of not more than:
50 penalty units for an individual; or
250 penalty units for a body corporate;
the manner in which notices, orders, directions, instructions or other documents under this Act may be given, issued or notified; and
the charging of fees in respect of any matters under this Act.

(2) Despite section 14 of the Legislation Act 2003, the regulations may make provision in relation to a matter by applying, adopting or incorporating, with or without modification, any matter contained in an instrument or other document:
as in force or existing at a particular time; or
as in force or existing from time to time;
even if the instrument or other document does not exist when the regulations come into operation.
The regulations may:
vest an eligible court with jurisdiction in a matter or matters arising under the regulations; and
provide for review of decisions under the regulations.

section.heading: Marine Orders

content.p: AMSA may, by legislative instrument, make an order (to be known as a Marine Order) with respect to any matter for which provision must or may be made by the regulations.
If a Marine Order is inconsistent with this Act, the Marine Order is of no effect to the extent of the inconsistency.
A reference to this Act in subsection (2) does not include a reference to a Marine Order.

(4) Despite section 14 of the Legislation Act 2003, a Marine Order may make provision in relation to a matter by applying, adopting or incorporating, with or without modification, any matter contained in an instrument or other document:
as in force or existing at a particular time; or
as in force or existing from time to time;
even if the instrument or other document does not exist when the Marine Order comes into operation.

section.heading: Vessels that become or stop being facilities etc.

content.p: AMSA may, by legislative instrument, make rules providing as mentioned in subsection (2) in relation to any of the following:
vessels that become or stop being facilities or parts of facilities;
persons on board or near such vessels;
activities that take place on board such vessels.
Rules made under subsection (1) may:
provide for the application, or continued application, of this Act with or without specified modifications in relation to a vessel, person or activity mentioned in paragraph (1)(a), (b) or (c); or
make provision of a transitional, application or saving nature in relation to the transition from:
the regime provided by this Act to a regime provided by a law covered by subsection (3); or
a regime provided by a law covered by subsection (3) to the regime provided by this Act;
for a vessel, person or activity mentioned in paragraph (1)(a), (b) or (c).
This subsection covers the following laws:
(a) the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Act 2006 and legislative instruments under that Act;
(b) a State PSLA (within the meaning of Part 6.9 of the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Act 2006) and regulations under a State PSLA;
(c) a Territory PSLA (within the meaning of Part 6.9 of the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Act 2006) and regulations under a Territory PSLA.
The rules may provide as mentioned in paragraph (2)(a) despite:
(a) the effect of sections 640 and 641 of the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Act 2006 apart from this section; and
anything else in this Act.
The rules may deal with inconsistency between the rules and a law covered by subsection (3), including by providing that the rules prevail over such a law to the extent of any inconsistency.
Paragraphs (2)(a) and (b) do not limit each other.
AMSA may make rules under subsection (1) only with the agreement of the Chief Executive Officer of the National Offshore Petroleum Safety and Environmental Management Authority.
In this section:
facility means:
(a) a facility within the meaning of Schedule 3 to the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Act 2006; or

a vessel in an area in relation to which section 641 of that Act applies that would be a facility within the meaning of that Schedule if the vessel were located at a site in Commonwealth waters for the purposes of paragraph 4(1)(a) or (5A)(a) of that Schedule.
State PSLA has the same meaning as in Part 6.9 of the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Act 2006.
Territory PSLA has the same meaning as in Part 6.9 of the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Act 2006.

section.heading: Regulations and orders under the Navigation Act 1912

content.p: (1) The regulations may provide for specified regulations and orders that were in force under the Navigation Act 1912 immediately before its repeal to have effect, for the purposes of this Act, with such modifications as are specified in the regulations.

(2) The Marine Orders may provide for specified orders that were in force under the Navigation Act 1912 immediately before its repeal to have effect, for the purposes of this Act, with such modifications as are specified in the Marine Orders.
